reviews.text:
1. Infrastructure is kind of dated.  For example, bathroom shower head is not fixated and water streams cannot be adjusted to the forward direction.  This made it very hard to shower hands free.

2. The toilet in my room leaks - there's always a small puddle on the left side of the toilet.

3. Very cheap stay - less than USD 50 a day with breakfast included.

4. Good location with city buses to HSR station and rail station.
Very clean place with friendly and helpful staff. Had a great overall experience—would definitely recommend!

Good for international travelers, great value for money. Helpful and professional staff members who speak good English.

Rooms are small, but modern and well-designed, with all the amenities you would expect. Very quiet, good mattresses, comfortable.

The extended breakfast buffet is nice, but clearly only intended for regional guests, and has little to offer for the more conservative Western traveler. In spite of what the name of the hotel implies, the food is certainly not kosher.

I’ve stayed here at least five times but still can’t figure out why it is called Talmud or why it is marketed as a “Jewish” themed hotel; it feels like a randomly chosen concept.

Recommended for travelers who want a quiet, unassuming and comfortable hotel for a good price.

A very nice hotel located in the small township. Customer service is excellent. Anticipating guest needs whenever seek.
Rooms for 2pax are comfortable but not to big. Basic amenities are available with reasonable quality. Beds are comfortable and clean.
Breakfast spread are simple and nice. Do be prepared to clear your own dishes and place them on the dish cart. You are also advice to separate your waste as per indicated. Taiwan is practising waste separation hence this hotel is adopting the practice. Service crew is also available around to clean the table after guest leave before anticipating another guest.
Just nearby there is a FAMILY MART convenient store. For the ladies whom are looking for facial essential, make up and mask essentials...there is also a store located just by this hotel and opens till 11pm.
Room is too small. You even cannot open your suitcase. Western style Breakfast was very very poor, just toast and marmalade. Chinese style seems to be ok.

reviews.text:
I had a pleasant stay at this hotel for two nights on April 4–5, 2025. The staff were incredibly friendly, especially 葉勳 (Ye Xun), who went above and beyond to help me arrange a haircut at a local barbershop (along with another kind lady).

I also accidentally left my silver ring behind, and Ye Xun kindly arranged for it to be delivered to my flat in London. What truly stood out was his passion for his job—he even mailed the ring on the same day I called for assistance.

Every member of the staff was nothing but helpful, making my stay truly enjoyable. Thank you for everything—I hope this feedback reaches them!

Stayed for 2 nights on 30 Nov and 1 Dec. Arrived at hotel before 1pm. We met this bad attitude young female receptionist. She told us to leave our luggage near the lift lobby by ourselves and come back at 3pm. Then she just left and went to the toilet.  What a "warm" welcome. We went to the 1st floor toilet after her and found the floor wet and disgusting.Fortunately when we came back to check-in later in the afternoon we were met by a friendly young male staff who also offered to  help us book a taxi to the train station when we checked out. The room spacious for 2 people, shower pressure good. Convenient location. Breakfast was basic.

Style and good location. The front desk staff was impressive - Ye Xun (業勳) was very friendly and helpful. He was very responsive to our needs and always had a smile on his face.

My boss stayed at several hotels during his business trip to Taiwan and also thought he was a very enthusiastic hotel employee (other staffs may need to be smiley and be friendlier XD)

Overall, it's value for money.

Good location and easy to get around with the buses. Although you really need the public transport app to know the times for the buses. You can’t rely on the published timetable. The room is decent but there are two issues I see. Firstly, the mini fridge doesn’t really get cold. It’s more of a cooler that keeps things cool, not cold. No thermostat so a but useless. The toilet has no floor to ceiling door. So the smell from the toilet will stay in the room for some time. If there are two of you, prepare for bad smells. This is not a good design but I see you are trying to be modern.

The staff are nice when checking in and for breakfast.

The room cleaning is extremely slow. We went out in the morning and it still wasn’t cleaned by 3pm. We ended up telling them to just give us towel and not worry about the room. When we arrived to go to the room at 3 pm ( check in time), the staff had to run upstairs before us to check if the room was done.

Also if you want the air conditioner lower than 23, just ring the front desk.

Lovely modern hotel next to walkable delicious food and historical attractions. My husband and I stayed a week here in the tatami room with our 1 and 4 year old. We were able to push the beds together to give them plenty of space to move since they are very active sleepers.

Everything was very clean and comfortable. The stay included a tasty breakfast each morning and local snacks and water in the room daily. Staff were very friendly, attentive and communicated very well though we only spoke English.

Traveling international was hard enough with littles, but this hotel made our stay easy. Very child friendly with toys in the room, high chair in the dining area, and stroller available for day use. Even with it being located on a busy street, it was not too noisy and my baby was able to nap well during the day. This will be our go to place to stay when we return!

reviews.text: This child friendly hotel suited our family holiday with great activities for the kids. They throughly enjoyed the train, driving track sandpit and water fountain. Rooms were clean, simple and comfortable.

Centrally located in town with Anping district just a few minutes by car away. The hotel is also located next to a shopping centre /super market so you can get snacks / food if you're too lazy to go far (especially with young kids).

The hotel is definitely catered to kids and level 4 (lobby), has an outdoor play area including a sand pit (clean white sand!), a train where parents & kids can hopped on (though there is a schedule), and electric cars which the kids can either ride themselves or parents can use a remote to control it. This opens at 8am and closes at 10pm so my 6-year old could spend the whole day there.

Level 5 is the indoor playground and split across different rooms. Another place where the kids can entertain themselves for a couple of hours.

Level 12 is the gym but it is fairly basic. 2 running threadmill, a stepper, and 2 bikes. The weights were kept behind locked doors.

Rooms are big and we had two queen size beds and enough space (and walking room) for a travel cot too. Amenities are unfortunately not available given environmental policy changes but there is a water dispenser at the lift lobby on the room floor.

Will certainly be back again if we come back to visit.

The price is almost the same level as Region but
The room is huge! Without a coffee machine, it makes people sad. Using instant coffee instead make it worse.
BF lacks of protein but, luckily the beef soup saved the total experience.

Stayed at Hotel Cozzi for 2 nights. We are a family of 3 (with 1 baby).

Pros -

- Centrally located, close to most attractions and a huge mall.
- Lots of eating options nearby on all ends of the cost spectrum.
- Large, comfortable well-lit rooms with great, soft beds. Our request for a baby cot was fulfilled.
- Large bath/toilet area with a Japanese toilet.
- Great for our baby, as there is an entire floor with 3 differently themed play areas. These are cleaned regularly, so it's great.
- Wifi was decent throughout.
- The entire hotel was cartoon themed, which our baby loved!

Cons -

- We opted for breakfast on the last day. The layout of the breakfast is a bit weird. Overall, the spread is good, but on a taste level, I'd say it was just ok. The eggs were soggy, the coffee was so-so. The fruit platter was fresh.
- Staff is helpful, but need to prod them to get more information or details about a facility.
- There is a laundry room, but it is paid. There's an accompanying seating area, which looks comfortable but the couches/bean bags need some cleaning.
Convenient location. Close to department store at the heart of the city. The room is spacious and clean. Only downside is that we couldn’t adjust the temperature for the air conditioner.

reviews.text: You’re not going to find a nicer place than this at this price. Massive room, modern, and super clean. Great location, too. Only downside was there wasn’t anywhere to refill our water bottles but the room does have a kettle to use. Would highly recommend staying here.

Good location. Easy check in although we didn't understand their msg regarding LINE until a helpful Taiwanese lady explained it was a messenging app we needed to download.
Bed very firm. Would not suit everyone.

Clean, great room. But the booking process needs to be streamlined. Several emails, phone calls, a bank transfer, finally a door code but no room number. It shouldn't have been so complicated. But the room is nice. Once you get in, you'll like it.

A super large and comfortable room. I was very comfortable during my time in Tainan. ❤️ Everything was very clean and the room was well-equipped. The owner was also very friendly and helped me with everything I needed during my stay. It's also in a great location, close to the center, many shops, and the train and bus stations. Highly recommended! :)

We stayed in a 4-person room on the second floor, which matched the room provided on the website.
Pros:
1. Spacious. I suggest adding photos of the bathroom on the website so they can be used as a reference when booking.
2. The B&B is located in the city, making it easily accessible.
3. We have a partnership with a car rental company and can offer a $50/day discount.
Cons:
1. Located near the road and on a low floor, it was quite noisy at night, with the constant whirring of motorcycles.
2. Due to environmental concerns, bottled water was not provided, but there was no water dispenser either, which was a bit inconvenient.
3. Self-check-in and check-out are done by inserting the key directly into the door. Since there is no floor control, I was concerned about intrusion by anyone other than the B&B owner before or after my stay. I recommend using a combination lock to store the key to prevent intrusion by anyone other than the person who booked the room.

reviews.text:
Exactly like the other reviews.

It's a rare opportunity to bring my parents to Tainan, but what happened?!

I was stunned upon entering the room...they're such homebodies!

Not to mention the homebodies themselves, the environment isn't particularly good 😭

I started to feel itchy halfway through my sleep and even saw tiny bugs.

My child has sensitive skin, so I really don't recommend this place.

The ladder in the room is so redundant!

There's no dressing table. After showering, I had to sit on the floor to blow dry my hair.

$3,350 per night on a holiday is incredibly expensive (and no one was staying).

And then there's the fact that they don't have parking. Besides the exorbitant room rate, you have to pay for parking yourself!

Street parking is a one-in-a-million chance (there aren't many spots). Parking in the remote area is really inconvenient...

The holiday parking next door is incredibly expensive, $60 an hour.

All in all, this was one of the worst experiences I've ever had in Tainan.

The helper responded quickly. 2,600 for a room for four on Saturday wasn't bad. Comments mentioned poor soundproofing, which was tolerable for just one night. However, upon entering the room, there was a strong smell of sewage. Even with a dehumidifier running, it was still very uncomfortable. 😓

The bathroom setup was also terrible. A shower curtain would be fine, but it should at least be floor-to-ceiling. Even if you shower inside, water still splashes all over the outside.

Most importantly, the room didn't feel very clean. My child and I both broke out in allergic rashes all over our legs. 😰😰😰

There was a large gap under the bathroom curtain, which couldn't stop the water from leaking out. The room was not soundproofed and the door made noises when it was opened and closed. Cockroaches ran out in the middle of the night, which made the hygiene questionable. The room was crowded, and there was a space like an upper bunk, which was very useless. The ladder was difficult to climb and you had to bend over the whole time to avoid hitting the ceiling.

If you're looking for a more comfortable accommodation in Tainan, check out other options right away.

And if you're a female, I highly recommend avoiding this unless you're comfortable with dim lighting, difficulty applying makeup, a lack of security, or running out of hot water mid-shower.

Self-service check-in is available.

We booked a comfortable room for four. Not only was there no hand soap in the room during the pandemic, but the lighting was also very poor, dim, and lacking external ventilation, making the overall experience quite stuffy.

The space was also very cramped, with poor circulation. The light switch was blocked by a decorative metal frame, and the refrigerator and sink were located in front of the bathroom entrance, so anyone trying to enter or exit would be hit.

The air conditioning wasn't cooling or heating. The remote control showed heating, but it wouldn't work when we tried. In winter, you'd be stuck under the covers.

The most incomprehensible thing was the bathroom.
That's the most important thing. You don't want to have a bad shower when you're out, right?

First, the shower and toilet are combined, with a mirror and vanity behind the toilet. With the mirror constantly reflecting back at you while you shower, how can you truly rest assured?

Also, above the showerhead, you can see a small, frosted glass that's clearly facing the outside, allowing you to see the shadows of things outside...

Furthermore, because we stayed in a shared room, the water heater stopped working after the previous guests showered. We were left without hot water until 4 or 5 in the morning, and by dawn, no one had finished showering.

The water pressure in the showerhead was also very inconsistent.

If they were truly dedicated, I doubt so many previous guests wouldn't have reported issues with the water heater and bathroom.

I can only say, please keep up the good work.

Don't neglect the equipment just to accommodate more guests.

The room had several signs of mold and minor damage.

The countertop inside the room was filled with cleaning supplies and amenities. There was a small wooden cabinet outside the room that held drinking water and other supplies, which was quite unsightly.

Regarding the environment: The area is adjacent to a land bridge, currently closed for construction, so the impact isn't significant. However, once it's repaired, it will likely be quite noisy, as other reviews have mentioned.

The window faces the Maitreya Temple across the street, so for those who might be bothered by this, please note.

The upside is that it's relatively affordable, and photography is possible inside.

Stayed in a quadruple room in the second building on 2023-02-24.
Entry and exit were via electronic locks, and communication with the staff was via Line.
The nearby footbridge was under demolition and closed during the holiday, so there was almost no traffic in front of the B&B, and I didn't experience the noise issues others had experienced.
The room had been cleaned the day before and was generally clean and odorless. There were three sinks, the most I've ever seen, and a full-length mirror by the door.
The bathroom and toilet were shared, with no separate wet and dry areas, a typical B&B design.
The location is less than 15 minutes from the Dadong Night Market. I recommend booking a stay with Dadawuhua. The walk to the Confucius Temple takes quite a while, so I definitely recommend booking a stay with the night market.
The service was prompt and attentive, with no issues.
The only downside was parking. There were no cooperating or relatively close options, so you had to find a paid parking spot. With luck, there might be roadside parking in the alley behind the B&B, but I didn't have the guts to find a parking lot. I personally recommend finding a 24-hour parking lot with a cap. Avoid the cash-only lot on Fulian Road. It's strictly for temporary parking. As soon as you enter, you have to pay for the first half hour, regardless of whether you park or not, and there's no cap. Look for a place that accepts electronic or online payments. If you have too much money, you can skip this part.

So, I only give the location four stars; it's a mixed bag.

reviews.text: Best hotel I made in the whole Taiwan. The room is so quite and nice, the staff is super friendly...I will come back here....

The room was new and clean, with no cigarette smell. The air conditioning was cold enough, and the hot water was powerful enough. The bed was a little firm for my taste. The front desk staff was friendly and helpful (and beautiful). Staying here made it hard to leave. There's motorcycle parking downstairs. The location is lively, and there are plenty of restaurants within walking distance. I look forward to visiting again.

I was very pleased with both the surroundings and the interior facilities! The lobby has plenty of seating, a kitchen, and a water dispenser, making it convenient to rest after a day out.

The room was very quiet and I slept very well. The bathroom was also spacious and had a bidet! The staff were very friendly and helpful, highly recommended!

There's parking for motorcycles.
Overall, it's good, but there's a 200 NTD charge for changing the sheets, as we've been told in advance. (If I remember correctly...)
Think about it, if someone stays one night a day, don't you have to change them too? Why is it so different for consecutive stays?
The first floor has a living room, oven, microwave, refrigerator, and water dispenser. Great~
The room isn't too small, and the wooden floors are great.
The air conditioner keeps dripping, so guests should be careful not to leave items under it.
The bathroom has a nice dry/wet separation, and the toilet has a bidet.
The overall color scheme is very soothing. 😌
Most importantly, there's a washing machine and dryer (detergent is available at the counter for 10 NTD). Each wash and dry takes 50 minutes, which is very convenient. 👍

The location is great, with many restaurants and attractions nearby (a 15-minute walk covers most of them). Although it's in an alley, it's a lively alley, so it's not too scary to walk back home at night. We had a street-view room, which was spacious, comfortable, and clean! The bed was a king-size and incredibly comfortable (although a bit firm). I couldn't get out of bed for two nights, haha. The bathroom had a bidet and separate wet and dry areas, and the water pressure was amazing! I think it was pressurized, which is why it's so strong. The only minor downside was that the toilet paper dispenser was a little difficult to use. The TV had a high resolution and was a perfect size, but the phone projector connection was sometimes unstable. The lobby has air conditioning and plenty of seating on the first floor, plus a microwave, popcorn oven, and toaster oven. I think the ample seating on the first floor is great, as it allows you to rest after checking out before heading out. Overall, it's a very nice cultural hotel, and I'd definitely stay there again.

reviews.text:
Decent size rooms and beds weren't bad. Has a coffee, tea, and dessert area where you can sit in the afternoons. It is not inconveniently located but not very close to sites and interesting areas.

Maple Hotel in Tainan offers a comfortable and affordable stay, perfect for both business and leisure travelers. Located in the city center, it provides easy access to major attractions, shopping areas, and public transportation, making it an ideal base for exploring the city. The hotel features modern, well-designed rooms that are clean and well-maintained, with comfortable beds and necessary amenities like free Wi-Fi, air conditioning, and flat-screen TVs.

Guests often highlight the hotel’s quiet atmosphere, making it a great choice for those looking for a peaceful retreat. The staff is friendly and attentive, always willing to assist with any requests or provide recommendations for local dining and attractions. Additionally, the hotel offers a simple breakfast buffet, which is a convenient option for guests starting their day.

While Maple Hotel may not offer the luxury of larger, high-end hotels, it provides excellent value for money. The facilities are basic but functional, and the rooms are a good size, ensuring a pleasant stay. Some guests have mentioned that the hotel could benefit from more variety in its breakfast options, but overall, it’s a solid choice for travelers looking for a clean, comfortable, and well-located hotel in Tainan.

Hotel is relatively old. Rather quaint.
Plus points: Bathroom is big, ample space; bed (king sized) is big; shower water pressure is good. There's a kettle in the room.

Not so great: bathroom has no mirrors; no safe in room; pillow way too soft and flat; duvet couldn't cover whole bed; cupboard has only 2 hangers; wifi unsecured and slow, keeps dropping; water takes way too long to get hot, waste of water.
Overall a not too bad but maybe look into the details.

The female receptionists are not friendly. The hotel claims to have Wi-Fi, but it doesn’t work at all. The room is very old, and the laundry service is not available within the hotel, making it very inconvenient. I would not recommend this hotel to my friends or relatives if they are visiting Tainan.

Our stay didnt started well: Awful service from the 2 people at the front desk, not welcoming and it was not even busy. The morning : the 2 girls were nice though, probably because we were already clients.

No wifi with code: hard to connect and stay connected. If you need to work: its a big NO go.

Glad our room was kinda great (except the hard matress), it was spatial, easy to park in the garage under the hotel & free bike to ride around town.
Cozy place, decent price. Good job. You can get a free snack in the first floor.

reviews.text:
The smell of cigarette smoke was immediately apparent upon entering. The check-in process was automated. The room was okay, but I killed several ants. The shower water was very small.

Will never stay again

Simple hotel~
Automatic check-in^^
Free parking for cars and motorcycles

I don't know the purpose of the shoe cabinet on the first floor
But you don't need to change shoes to enter the room

Nearby night market and McDonald's
Convenience store is a bit far away haha

If you take a bus to Tainan Transfer Station
Walk the small road for more than 10 minutes
Not far

Honestly, it was a very uncomfortable stay. The room had a moldy, dirty floor, and they even used disposable items. There were no bedside tables. The only positive thing was the soft bed.

The refrigerator was a small one shared by the entire floor. It looked like it hadn't been cleaned in years. There were stains and some semi-liquid residue, I don't know what it was. The trash can was at the first-floor stairwell, and there were cigarette cases in the elevator. It looked like someone was renting the place monthly, and many people who looked like they were working 8+9 were smoking outside, which was not a very pleasant experience. The exposed wires in the ceiling made me worried about something happening.

The most annoying thing was being woken up before dawn. At 4:50 a.m., I was startled by a child's screams and what sounded like their father's voice. Then, they were noisily closing the door and going downstairs. I don't know if it was luggage or something rolling down, but there was a loud thud. Then, I was woken up again at 6 or 7 a.m. My sleep quality was terrible, and I didn't even get to make up for my vacation.

The good thing is that there are a few attached parking spaces (but they were all gone by 9 PM...). The location is quite busy, but there are people parking right at the entrance to the fire lane, making it incredibly difficult to find a spot and get out...

The hotel is fully self-service. Overall, I won't be returning.

Because it's cheap, the decoration is acceptable. It's clean, and the bed is soft and comfortable. The main problem is the door of the room. It should be more secure. There can be an internal lock in the room, so that people who stay here can rest assured. The location is easy to find in the alley, but it's too big for a car with good driving skills. It may be difficult for those with poor driving skills. Oh, and the sound insulation is really not good. Light sleepers must bring earplugs.

There were big cockroaches in the room, the public toilet downstairs was full of ants and dirty, the bed was very itchy, my whole body was itchy, not very clean... The soundproofing was very poor, very poor, I could even hear the neighbors chatting, taking a shower, and opening and closing the door
Great location... parking available! ! The nearby attractions are all within a 10-minute drive away...
But it’s really not clean! The switches in the room leak electricity, and I get up to turn on and off the lights all night.

reviews.text: It's very close to Anping Old Street. The room, toilet, and bathroom are very clean. The main door and room doors all have electronic locks. There's an elevator in the B&B, which is very convenient for moving luggage. The room has many sockets, which is very convenient. Check-in and check-out are self-service (which I really like ☺️). Communication with the housekeeper by phone or online is very smooth. The environment is very quiet. It was a great stay!

There is a large TV in the living room, which is very convenient and enjoyable whether you are singing KTV or playing video games. There is also an electric mahjong table for playing. The kitchen is well stocked with kitchenware and seasonings, and the refrigerator is also very large.

The B&B facilities are quite clean and nice.

However, the B&B's management isn't so smooth.

Recently, your B&B ran a promotion offering NT$100 off for every 5-star review.
However, perhaps my review didn't live up to the B&B's standards (perhaps I wasn't too complimentary?).
So, after review, I didn't receive the NT$100 discount.
Whether or not there was a discount isn't a big deal, but the B&B's haphazard approach to the promotion really dampened our enjoyment.
If they're so fussy about even the promotion, then they might as well not have it at all.
Or, please provide a standard reply so we can copy and paste it. 🙂 It's really a bad experience. I hope the B&B can improve. Thank you.

Response on December 27
I'm not writing such a long review just because I'm bored 😂
I originally gave the B&B 5 stars and a Facebook like, as per the B&B's rules. The group leader compiled photos of the likes and sent them to the B&B. However, I later discovered that the B&B didn't reward me for my review or content. Does this mean my review isn't eligible? That was a truly disappointing experience.
That's why I changed my original five-star review with photos to this one. Your B&B could cancel this promotion or make some minor improvements. I believe that future improved promotions will improve the experience for even more guests!
*Attached is the original like and five-star review.

The boss is really nice 🥹🥹

What really makes this hotel stand out is the location. You’re just steps away from Dihua Street’s shopping scene, the traditional Yongle Market, and the famous Ningxia Night Market. It’s also about a 5-minute walk to the MRT, so getting around is super easy. I booked through the Klook app for around $100 CAD per night, which felt fair.

I skipped the hotel breakfast because there are just too many incredible local spots nearby to justify staying in. One unexpected bonus was a free shuttle tour to Jiufen included with the booking—well worth it and a great way to spend the day.

If you’re into nightlife or craft cocktails, there are two must-visits close by. Taku-Syaku is a gem for whiskey lovers. The owner, Young, is incredibly passionate and knows his spirits inside and out. Antique Bar 1900 is another standout. Step inside and you’re transported to a lush Victorian-era setting with an exclusive taste of French absinthe.

Lastly, MUST VISIT THE COFFEE SHOW AROUND THE CORNER!!!! If you’re a coffee fanatic you’ll LOVE the pour over experience.

All in all, the hotel itself is pretty average, but if you’re here for the location, food, and access to unique local spots, it’s a solid choice.

reviews.text: This hotel is conveniently located near the subway, making everything easily accessible. The room was simple yet clean, and all the staff members were friendly. I stayed 3 nights in a standard double room at RF Hotel. Overall, I’d say it’s a decent option for budget-conscious travellers who want a convenient, no-frills base in Taipei.

Check-In & Lobby:
The lobby was clean and inviting, with a pleasant vibe. Check-in was smooth and straightforward and my room was ready on arrival. Staff were friendly and accommodating throughout the stay.

Room:
The room was of standard size, clean, and functional. It may have been retrofitted at some point. There was a desk, a chair, a small bar fridge (that didn’t really work), and a TV with local channels. The aircon was strong and cold. Some light switches were almost broken and could use maintenance.

Noise levels were reasonable, but it’s worth noting that although the hotel is non-smoking, someone was clearly smoking on one of the mornings. The bathroom was serviceable, though the toilet’s fan ventilator brought in a sewage smell at times and switching it off helped.

Location:
This is where RF Hotel shines. From the airport, you can take the express train to Taipei Main Station, then walk through the underground mall to the blue MRT line and ride just four stops. The area has plenty of food, convenience stores, an underground mall, and cafés all nearby.

Facilities & Wi-Fi:
Wi-Fi was a major downside as it was almost non-existent in my room (which faced the back of the building). Phone reception was terrible too; I had to go down to the lobby to get decent signal and Internet.

However, there’s a useful common area with a microwave, water dispenser (cold and hot), coffee machine, instant beverages, and occasionally some snacks. Luggage is stored in a communal space under surveillance. Housekeeping, if requested, usually happens in the late afternoon. The shared study area is a plus, with ample power points for laptop use.

Would I Stay Again?
Probably, especially if I’m travelling on a budget and the price is right. It’s good value for money, given the prime location and friendly staff. Just don’t expect fast Wi-Fi in the room.

The RF Hotel in Zhongxiao Dunhua is not a hotel. It is a government health inspection waiting to happen. It is a cautionary tale wrapped in mold spores and misrepresentation. If you are looking for an experience that simulates the living conditions during a Victorian-era cholera outbreak, congratulations. You’ve found it.

We booked a room that looked, online, like something out of a budget lifestyle magazine. What we got looked like a set from a low-budget zombie film minus the charm. The photos were bait. The room was the switch. Even the room names were different on their website versus Agoda and Booking.com, possibly to create just enough confusion to legally gaslight you into accepting any random closet they assign.

No safe, despite being listed. Breakfast was advertised as “great,” but somehow wasn’t part of our booking. Clarity? Transparency? That’s for amateurs. The room itself was a masterpiece of decay: wallpaper peeling off like a bad sunburn, wood trims splintering like they gave up on life, and a side table so misaligned it looked like it had survived a minor earthquake. And the lighting? Grim. The room had a few pin lights, but it was still dark — nothing like the bright, welcoming room in the pictures. There was no lamp, no bedside lighting, no warmth. It was the kind of gloom that makes you question your life choices.

And the smell. Oh, the smell. It hits you the moment you enter the floor. Think wet laundry left inside a gym bag during monsoon season, then lovingly fermented for three days. Inside the room, you get a momentary illusion of cleanliness, shattered the instant you move anything. We pulled apart the twin beds, awkwardly bolted to a shared headboard like some weird marital punishment, and discovered dust bunnies the size of small rodents. Clearly, that area hadn’t seen a vacuum since the before times.

The bathroom? Regrouted, yes. But mold proudly made its appearance on the ceiling, likely because the shower’s “ventilation” is a decorative suggestion. Water droplets from a shower taken eighteen hours ago were still clinging to the walls, like survivors.

Now let’s talk about the air-conditioning, that invisible assassin. Centralized, and clearly never cleaned, it distributed dust like it was seeding a new civilization. Every morning we would wake up sneezing and coughing, which would magically vanish the moment we stepped outside, where the air was miraculously cleaner. And thanks to the pin lighting, you could literally see the dust suspended in the air, dancing like triumphant pathogens.

As for the “free drinks,” those were restocked with the regularity of a lunar eclipse. The staff? Getting their own from a filthy backroom that made me reconsider every communal space I’ve ever trusted. Speaking of communal areas, don’t bother. If you’re not inhaling mold, you’re swatting mosquitoes like it’s an Olympic sport. Staff watched us struggle and did nothing. Maybe they were placing bets.

When we asked for an extra pillow, you know, the bare minimum in the 21st century. It was handed over with the enthusiasm of a civil servant one week from retirement. The only person who ever smiled was the cleaner, bless her heart. But even she was no match for the sheer entropy of the place.

The price? Decent. The damage to our health? Extensive. We went through allergy pills, cough meds, and an existential reckoning. This place is not just unsanitary. It’s a deathtrap. A biohazard masquerading as accommodation. The Taiwanese government should inspect it immediately. Or better yet, condemn it.

If you’re booking this place, consider this your warning. Or your will.

Good location, nice cafes restaurants etc nearby.

The lobby had cockroaches, the bedroom wasn't soundproof, and the people in the adjacent room, who were Taiwanese, slammed their door loudly at 1 a.m. for three consecutive nights, causing me to wake up startled each time. They spoke very loudly and were extremely rude. Informing the staff didn't improve anything. It was a nightmare for me, and I won't be returning to Taipei again because I am disappointed with the people's manners here.

This place is filthy and disgusting. We stayed in room #1205 and the room smelled like urine everywhere! Also the heater doesn’t work well. Worst part of this hotel is basic amenities are not met and the hotel falsely advertise online. I was taking shower and after 30 second there was no hot water at all! Hotel also gives you only one key when you are traveling with another person! Lobby also smells disgusting. The whole building smells like old feet. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone! Also hotel asks you to pay cash instead of credit card. This is far the worst hotel in Taipei.

Choose the 11th floor if you choose to stay here. I got the room #1103. It was good with bath tub. The room rate was reasonable.

However, my friends booked the room here and got the room on the 6th floor. It smells really bad, old, and low ceilings.

BY ALL MEANS DO NOT STAY HERE. IT IS DANGEROUS. There was a man trying to open our room at 5am and his card WORKED!!

I stayed there twice; both times, I reserved the room that appears on the website with a new bathroom, carpet floor, renovated room, etc. Both times, they gave me rooms that were old, with linoleum floors, old bathrooms, and weird beds. I asked to change the rooms both times, and they agreed. However, the first time, they asked me to pay an additional 300 NTD. Overall, the staff is friendly and ready to answer any questions. However, the hotel isn't worth it. The location is just okay, not that close to the subway or any good sightseeing spots.

!!!!
The craziest part, however, is that the second time I stayed there, a man opened my door with his card key at 5 am! I yelled in fear, and he left. I suspect all card keys on the second floor are the same and can open any door. So be aware!

reviews.text: This hotel is located in the street at the exit of Dongmen mrt station. It is a very good location. There is a morning market selling food and groceries and a 7-11 next to the hotel. The staff is very friendly. My room has some peeling on the walls, but it doesn’t bother me at all because the room is quite clean. The only downside I found is poor noise insulation. You can hear the outside noise quite clearly. But overall, this is a good hotel at a budget price.
I found the reception staff to be kind as well. I had a comfortable stay. One small issue was the shower temperature control, which was a bit tricky to figure out.

Room has all the essentials, including AC and a fridge however there was a shortage of storage space meaning the couch had to be used to put things on. That is literally the only negative I can draw. The staff were great and the location is excellent - you can be on the MRT in just minutes from leaving your room.
Also CKS memorial hall is only a very short walk away too.

“You get what you pay for” is true to this place. However, we paid for its posted price NT2400+ 400(tax), almost $3000, not the discounted price on some search engines for NT 2000 or lower…

Pros: great location. Their interior design looks good, and there’re water dispenser on each floor. Their reschedule or cancellation policy is flexible.

Cons: this room has a moldy wall that needs to be fixed and maintained! The bathroom wall is moldy also. The floor is not clean, especially filthy near the corners. Like some other reviews mentioned, there’s NO elevator and our room was on the 4th floor!! If you are traveling with small kids, elderly, or huge suitcases, consider triple times before booking. The sound proofing is also not good, you can here your neighbors talk. The window does not close properly so we can here what’s going on from the street.

This hotel has lots of potential but needs to be maintained properly!

we were very disappointed with this hotel. you could clearly see that it has not been cleaned very well for a long time. the floors were dirty, full of dust and long hairs. there were several yellow stains and hairs on the bedsheets (we guess they have not been changed or cleaned well). also we slept very badly because the sound insulation was very poor (you could hear everything from the streets outside and the corridors). there was no warm water in the shower so we had to shower with ice cold water. the towels also had yellow stains and big (!!) holes in them!!! they looked very old. the walls were full of marks and the wallpaper was coming down. there was mould on the ceiling and in the bathroom. the corridors of the hotel were full of big messy boxes and many things were lying around. additionally the water dispenser was very very very dirty and disgusting and my friend got food poisoning from drinking the water.
this hotel was by far the worst hotel experience we had in our lives and it was a very bad ending to our trip to Taiwan. we really did not enjoy our stay and even considered moving to another hotel for the night as everything was so disgusting and dirty. i am literally feeling sick just by thinking about the hotel room. if possible, do not stay here. i strongly recommend choosing another hotel as the stay here is truly not enjoyable. i've listed just the major things, there is honestly much more to complain about. very disappointing, never again.

reviews.text: I really enjoyed my stay here, especially as my first time ever being in Taiwan! The room I stayed in was clean, and it was nice that the beds each had curtains to make it feel a bit more private. The one tour I joined, led by PC, was also super nice and everyone who participated was also a joy to talk to. PC did a wonderful job showing us around and I almost wish the tour would’ve been longer! Location-wise this Hostel is perfect as it’s right next to Ximen and also has a close metro nearby. Only note I have to give was that somehow everytime I wanted to take a shower there were no (clean) shower mats in the basket anymore, but that’s a small issue. Overall, I was surprised this hostel only counts as 2 stars because it definitely deserves more, I’d certainly come back again!

Staff here are amazing. Hostel has big open lobby for easy repacking. Laundry available and shared kitchen with free coffee, water and tea! Staff were so kind to help us store our luggage as we continued with the rest of our travels. So thankful for meander and its staff!

This place was a solid 5 star in every category except for one issue: the bunk bed mattress. It was so soft it bottomed out completely with a loud thud offering no lumbar support to my back. It's surprising no other reviewer had mentioned this fact. So it may be  possible that people do actually like very soft mattresses. A quick note to the staff: The hand towel by the common area sink was soaked with water every time I tried to use it. Replacing it more often would be a huge help. A shout out to the exceptionally professional stuff. Thank you all.

We had such a wonderful stay! Everybody's so nice, friendly, and accommodating - from the receptionist to the housekeepers. The rooms are clean, the whole ambiance of the hostel is so homie and comfortable. The common area is spacious and can house 30-50 guests all at once. It's a nice place to mingle with guests from all over the world. It's location is also very strategic - near supermarkets, convenience stores and Ximending if you're inti shopping. It's really highly recommender. Will definitely come back if I get the chance.

Meander Taipei Hostel offers a clean, beautifully designed space with a welcoming atmosphere. The rooms smell fresh and are kept in excellent condition, making the stay both relaxing and enjoyable. Highly recommended for travelers seeking comfort and cleanliness.

reviews.text:
right next to ningxia market-

very well maintained when i stayed 13-14jun2025 - everything is good -

even there is a sink for manual washing + a wringer can be used free of charge

- it would be better to add a small table in the living room near the kitchen so you can eat there

I picked this hotel for it's convenient location to where I needed to be early morning next day. I was a little concerned about the self check-in, as sometimes those things can go wrong. Luckily, this wasn't the case with this hotel. The self check-in machine was fairly straightforward to use, and once I checked in, I had to find a staff member to receive my room key. There was an option of renting a locker, but since I wasn't leaving the hotel in the evening, and departing super early the next morning, I didn't rent one.

The room itself is small, but comfortably spacious with interesting and convenient arrangement of the beds. The bathroom wasn't too far and was clean with warm water available. The hotel is quite big, but it is sectioned, so it is not difficult to navigate around, or find the closest kitchen area, lounge area, or the bathroom.

I really enjoyed my stay here, and if I need to stay in the area again, I will most certainly come back.

The only downside of staying here is the number of loo and shower they have - they have plenty of dormitory rooms which means guests and it's gonna be packed during peak hours (before 8am and after 8pm) - and the absence of luggage lockers for the guests (in your dorm room you'll just leave your luggage nearby or down if you're at the top bunk then pray nobody will get it. Kudos they have a hanger where you can hang your wet towel.

Just a few minutes walk from the nearest MRT station.

Their breakfast buffet is superb!! Plenty of choices -- they label vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes!! Something recommended!

They also allow you to leave your luggage with them after you checkout and come get it later!

The room was good and tidy but small. breakfast: they falsely labelled meat dumplings as vegetarian. The milk tea and orange juice are too sweet for my taste. No water was provided at the buffet, but there is a water dispenser near the elevator. Staff was friendly. Location was good.
great hotel right next to ning xia night market!! only docking a star because the showerhead didn’t work in the stall i used…

reviews.text:
I would say this is a nice hotel but not for fussy people. Room is small but its just nice for a cabin luggage. There’s no elevator so u have to carry up through the narrow stairs. It’s only three storeys high and it’s very convenient as it’s directly across the subway station. There’s both 7-11 and familymart below the hotel and some food stores along/outside the subway station! The downside of this place is that they will not clean your room till the day you check out, and on some days they might not replenish the bottled water or toiletries. Check in also takes some time as there’s no reception so it’s a virtual check in through LINE.
All in all it’s an affordable and nice place if your not fussy!

Worst customer service I’ve ever had in my life. A person who was in charge of the customer service on 13th, August, 2024 made me wait outside in a humid and hot weather for an hour excusing he would check my email I replied but never checked and never sent me any information for check-in. I sweated a lot and even was almost dehydrated. I managed to add line ID and sent my info. but I ended up staying other hotel unexpectedly without any notice from him. He never called me and never replied my request for check-in. Good location but worst customer service it has.

Clean and location friendly hotel/apartment.

Only downside is that it’s a bit small but that’s no biggie considering the room is just for sleeping and shower.

The AC works great, clean, water bottles available daily and fresh towels too. Bonus is they water pressure is amazing  probably the strongest I’ve ever experienced ever. I stayed at room 301 for reference.

Experience is seamless with the phone at the front door. Just follow instructions and you can’t go wrong. Would recommend!

First check in very comfortable and accessible to all. 2nd check in we can't sleep at night to much dust we sneeze and cough, i dont know where the dust came from but when i check the aircon very dusty so i think aircon needs to be cleaned also. Thank you

It was generally good.
Stayed in single room.
Room is not too big or small. Suitable for single person traveler who prefers to have personal room and toilet.
Not suitable for someone with bulky luggage as the room is not big enough to fit it in.
Dusty.
Only stairs. Therefore people with heavy luggage need to carry the luggage all the way up the stairs.
Would be a bit difficult for tall people as the ceiling is not high.
Not easy to spot its entrance.
Located at a place where food and daily utensils are easily accessible.

reviews.text: My 3rd times here! Highly recommended to anyone who wants to stay in a boutique hotel! Make sure have their signature breakfast (a la carte style)!

The highlight for me was the 5 to 6pm “wine hour” where basically they have free flow on the floor - they put the bottles there and in case you need a refill just call the receptionist. During our stay they provided sake on our floor for both pf the nights.

Rooms: they are small but I found the mattress and pillows to be very good for me.
Toilet is great too with hi-tech toilet seat.

Some reviews are talking about hearing the neighbours, we didn’t have this problem. Our room was facing the back of the building abd it was extremely quiet (not sure if it’s the same for the main road facing rooms).

Location: quite centrally positioned but a 10-15 min walk to a MRT station.

No facilities like gym or swimming pool.

We didn’t eat at their famous restaurant this time.

All in all this has been a great hotel and I would definitely return. Book in advance for better prices.

My one-night stay at the Musa Hotel was a truly enjoyable experience.

What I loved:
* The convenience of having a Michelin-starred restaurant on the lower floor for breakfast was a fantastic start to the day.
* The hotel's decor struck a perfect balance of understated modern elegance and cleanliness, with the room featuring beautiful wooden flooring, excellent natural light, and a comfortable bed.
* The unique concept of different wine-themed collaborations on each floor added a special touch to my stay. Daily Happy Hour (5:00 PM-6:00 PM) allowed us to savor limited-edition wines from these themed wineries.
* The rooftop bar had a relaxed atmosphere, and the service was exceptional.
What I didn't love:
* Unfortunately, the soundproofing in the room was lacking, and I could hear the crying of the kid next door, which was quite bothersome.

Overall, Musa Hotel offers one of the best staycation experiences in Taipei, making it a definite recommendation for couples seeking a short, relaxing escape.

When planning for my trip to Taipei after more than 3 years a hiatus of traveling, this hotel did draw my attentions was the wine and dine. I arrived the hotel in the early afternoon, the staff let me to do the check-in procedure first. It was fast and smooth. Since the room wasn’t ready, I just left my luggage at the concierge. I stepped out to have a coffee and snack. My room was ready when I came back to the hotel 90 minutes later and my luggage had already delivered there.

I booked a Urban Deluxe Room with City view. Room was very clean and bright with decent size. The amenities are very nice. The closet located at the entrance but also be able to access from the bathroom, so it was very convenient to get ready in the morning. The bed was very comfy!

One of the highlights of this hotel is the free “Wine O’clock” from 17:00-18:00 at the Super Bar of each floor, also snacks bar with all sort of candy bars, sweets, cookies, coffee, tea and bottle water…were available 24 hours. Guest can enjoy the fine wines from 7 super wineries from 6 countries. Unfortunately I didn’t make the reservation with their Michelin 2 star restaurant Molina de Urdániz which is the big highlight of Hotel Mvsa!

Staff are very polite and friendly! I didn’t hear too much of the noises from street even though it’s next to highway. Overall, my stay was very enjoyable! Definitely it’s highly recommended to any people into wine and dine!

I had a wonderful surprised with the upgrade to Winery Deluxe Room during my stay. Room was very spacious with a long window bench and a deep soaking bath tub, separate shower & Japanese smart toilet. A large wardrobe with safety box was placed  right next to the entrance. Bed was large queen size bed.

The best part of my stay is the breakfast. I tried three main dishes and the are all good.
Few suggestions:
1. Restaurant staff should not keep touching their masks (one person did it very often during my breakfast & lunch); 2. All drinks in the room are too sweet. I need low sugar content soft drinks; 3. Need to response email or LINE faster ( under staff, I think); 4. The meat dishes of lunch menu is under salt

reviews.text:
My partner and I recently stayed at Caesar Park Hotel Taipei, and we were both pleasantly surprised by its excellent location and great value for money.

The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful, especially David, who always greeted us with a bright smile and made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived.

Our room was clean, tidy, and comfortable, and when we had a small issue with the toilet, it was resolved immediately by the maintenance team — very impressive service!

The hotel’s location couldn’t be more convenient, being directly across from Taipei Main Station and right above the MRT lines, which made getting around the city incredibly easy.

The only minor challenge was finding the hotel entrance at first — the large complex it’s housed in can be a bit confusing. Once we figured it out, though, everything else was smooth sailing.

Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would happily recommend Caesar Park Hotel Taipei to family and friends.

Keep smiling, David — you made our stay even more enjoyable!

Our stay at this hotel was okay, but there’s definitely room for improvement.

Cons:
We found dark hair on our towels twice, which was quite disappointing. Each person only gets one pillow, the gym is poorly equipped and the walls aren’t soundproof — we could clearly hear doors closing and noises from the corridor. The elevators are very slow and there aren’t enough of them. To reach the gym or pool, you actually have to change elevators, which is quite inconvenient.
Even though I specifically asked about the pool in advance, the staff didn’t mention the daily disinfection times (the pool closes twice a day for a full hour) or that swimming caps are mandatory. You can’t even buy one directly at the pool — you have to go all the way to the reception to purchase it for 100 TWD.
Breakfast was large in variety, but unfortunately not very tasty or special.

Pros:
There was a surprisingly wide variety of vinegars at breakfast, water dispensers on every floor, cozy spots in the room to sit and enjoy the city view and a free parking lot.

Overall, it’s an average stay — some nice touches, but the cleanliness, communication, and facilities could be much better.

We had a room on one of the highest floors, the view was great and at first sight the room was nice too. But the closer we looked, the more details we found that were just not what you'd expect in a 5 star hotel. The windowsill was dirty, the ceiling over the window had spots and random stuff hanging out, the fabric of the walls around the bed was starting to fall off.
The bathroom was spacious but a very small tub for an expensive room (hotel pictures show big tubs) and the toilet had a constant bad smell to it, the flush handle was loose as well.
We wanted to go to the pool, which is only accessible through stairs, no elevator to that level, and it was full with kids yelling and playing. It was evening so i expected something a little more quiet. Also, there was a safety guard watching over the pool, although the pool was shallow enough to stand in it. I did not feel comfortable going for a swim with a person constantly watching me.
The staff was friendly and the lobby is impressive, but it was just not what i expected based on the pictures and the price we paid.

Location is great, as it’s directly across from Taipei station. Plenty of convenience stores, night markers, and shops nearby. However, the room itself was extremely disappointing; it was very outdated and in need of a renovation. Also, there were no plugs next to the bed. The room was also very dusty.

The position is great if you travel to and from the main station. It is also good that the hotel’s elevator takes you to the train/subway station. Rooms are old, poorly maintained, which you would not expect from a 5 star hotel. Staff not very kind and low quality food at the breakfast buffet.

reviews.text:
Title: Terrible service attitude – breakfast felt like being watched, staff hoarding food for themselves?

We stayed at this hotel with four family members. The facilities and environment are indeed nice, but our entire experience was ruined during breakfast because of the staff’s shocking attitude.

Breakfast dishes ran out early, vegetables were gone and never refilled, and the staff simply didn’t care. When we took some pork floss to go with our rice, a female staff member in a green uniform wearing glasses openly and loudly mocked us in front of other guests, saying: “I don’t know why there are so many people who love pork floss today!” This was extremely disrespectful and humiliating.

Even worse, we later personally saw male and female staff using lunch boxes to pack up the remaining dishes and fruits for themselves. At the same time, they were discussing “which dishes ran out” and “who took too much.” We paid NT$200 per person for breakfast (NT$800 for four people), yet we were treated like we were being monitored while eating. If the staff cannot stand guests taking food, then don’t charge for breakfast and just keep it for themselves!

To make things worse, breakfast service ends at 9:00 a.m., but the staff kept pushing us to finish quickly long before that, repeatedly reminding us that they were about to “clean up and get off work.” Other hotels allow guests to finish their meals at their own pace even after service ends, but here we felt completely rushed, as if we were unwelcome.

We left angry and disappointed. The hotel’s hardware is beautiful, but the staff’s mindset is completely wrong. It even strongly feels like the reason dishes were not refilled was simply because the staff wanted to keep the leftovers for themselves or their families.

We strongly suggest the owner check the security camera footage from the breakfast shift that day. You will clearly see what your employees were doing and how they treated paying guests.

If you ever wonder why this hotel’s business isn’t doing well, look no further – this kind of staff attitude is the root cause.

3 adults booked and provided with 1 double and 1 single bed for 5nights. Cleaning done only once as noted; while we asked for the "cleaning" request on the door wall, the cleaning service was not offered. The amenities are self-service from the frontdesk.

We stayed for 5 nights with the breakfast included, paying about 900 USD for 3 adults.

Breakfast was not as attractive as I expected for this price.  A few Taiwanese food are changing everyday with very limited varieties in dishes basically. The chubby man manager keeps watching the customers eating.

Frontdesk staff are overall friendly.  The woman manager is multilingual and thus helpful.

Location:  5 mins from airport Limousin bus stop, public bus statations are also nearby. From Taiwan main station, it will take about 40 mins on foot.

The bed headboard is dusty on top and walls are thin between rooms, can hear other guests talking loudly and screaming. The tv is quite bad and blur, seems slightly spoilt. However, room is spacious and comes with a bath-tub in the 3room, a new city view too. Would recommend for those who is staying for few days.

Room was way bigger than expected. All of their personnel were friendly to us, very professional and proficient in English.

He rooms were incredibly cleaned and equipped with toiletries, closet, slippers, good amount of towels, and a safe!!

The bed were very comfortable and the pillows were surprisingly soft. The blanket es a feather blanket and they also had TV cable.

Two bottles of water + tea included in this spacious room. Will definitely be back and come here only for my trips to Taipei.

Convenient location with helpful and friendly receptionist. Some of the receptionist even speaks Japanese.

Moreover, their room was super clean and well-equipped with all the necessities.

Overall, for this standard of service for this price range, I would highly recommend.

reviews.text: My husband and I had a wonderful stay at this hotel! The staff were welcoming, and  ready to help. The room was clean, comfortable, and well-maintained throughout our stay. The location was also convenient—close to key attractions and easy to get around. What really stood out was the attention to detail and the excellent service. I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to anyone visiting the area.

Industrial deco hotel. I had a single bed in a cozy room. Loved the actual hotel stay.  However, I personally didn't think the add-on breakfast was worth the extra money. Could probably get better food with the same amount of money or less at other places nearby, after all you are at the heart of the city here.

So yeah, 100% recommend the hotel, but suggest you skip the breakfast option if it cost ya extra.

Super cozy yet low key hotel. The staff are very friendly and keen to help. I love the aesthetic of the hotel. The rooms were nice and comfortable. The lounge area was nice to chill and hang out. Great location also. Within walking distance to shops, markets, MRT stations. Very convenient and pleasant stay indeed. Highly recommended both for holiday and work related stay.

I’m not sure how to feel about this hotel. It seems incredibly pricey for what you get. The staff are all miserable and create no connection with staying guests, check in felt more like an airport with the queue almost out of the door. They are very strict with the 3pm check in which I can understand, but the attitude towards guests asking to check in even 30 minutes early is unacceptable. The rooms are mid to small sized and ours smelt so damp. There was mold in the shower and all of the fabric in the room smelt of it too so it’s no doubt lurking in hidden places. There was no window in our room and it just felt awfully dark and uncomfortable, I don’t think the industrial/prison like design of the hotel was really helping with that either. The only thing that was actually quite good is the diy laundry which is simple enough to use, it cost $70 to wash and $50 to dry.

We checked in as a party of four (including two elderly guests) with two rooms. Below is a summary of our overall experience at the hotel.

Location

The hotel is located close to a bustling shopping area but quite a distance from the station, which may not be ideal during the rainy season, travelling with more than one elderly or you have a big luggage case.

Cleanliness / Miscellaneous

One of the rooms assigned was located deep within the building, and getting there felt like navigating a maze each time.

The bedsheets had noticeable stains.

The trolley used for towels was covered in rust.

The room were small, especially if you have large luggage.

The TV was faulty.

The hotel’s water piping system was poor — there was a lingering toilet smell and the pipes frequently made loud noises.

Service

It was challenging to request a room change unless there was a very valid reason. One staff was unwilling to change our room, stating that the hotel was fully booked. (Big relief for our elderly pair when they could finally switched their maze room for a better one located near the lift at the end.)

The front desk staff were rather cold if not rude when we simply asked about the possibility of a late checkout (by about 2–3 hours). Another staff member openly told the colleague we were speaking with to always reject such requests, in front of us.

On a positive note, we appreciated the housekeeping team for their prompt service recovery when we requested fresh towels. Although the room change took days, we are sincerely thankful for this assistance.

reviews.text:
A Timeless Gem in the Heart of Taipei - The Grand Hotel 圓山大飯店

Staying here was an unforgettable experience! This iconic luxury hotel, perched majestically on a hill in the center of Taipei, offers a perfect blend of rich history and vintage charm. Loved by many foreign travelers, the hotel’s striking red and jade décor creates an elegant and grand atmosphere both inside and out.
From the moment I stepped into the lobby, I was captivated by the exquisite interior design and the welcoming vibe. The shops and restaurants inside the hotel also lived up to the high standards, offering everything you could wish for. The staff were incredibly friendly, professional, and helpful-some spoke English fluently, which made communication smooth and easy.
A small downside was the presence of mosquitoes, likely due to the lush trees and grass surrounding the hotel. The hotel cleverly combats this with mosquito-repelling doors that close firmly to keep them out, along with aroma lights that help banish mosquitoes indoors-definitely thoughtful touches.
I also heard from local friends that many celebrities have stayed here, including the legendary Jackie Chan, which adds to the hotel's famous status.
Overall, The Grand Hotel is a stunning place that I absolutely loved. I would definitely visit again if given the chance and highly recommend it to anyone traveling to Taipei. A true blend of history, luxury, and hospitality!

Spent a week here and I think I would consider staying here again. Compared to other hotels it would be considered more costly I think, but sometimes you get what you pay for. I have stayed in many hotels around the world, some historical like this one, but this was just so pleasant in many ways.

The food was amazing, slecetion, preparedness, quality, flavours, etc. Chow time was spot on.

The staff so nice to be aroud.

The grounds are just beautiful and Ienjoyed walking around outside, even though it was SO HOT!!!!!!!

I should have gone into the tunnels, but forgot.

Due to it's location it is great for day trips north as it has quick easy access to major roads.

View, amazing!

Grand Hotel Taipei (圓山大飯店) is more than just a hotel — it’s a cultural and historical landmark in Taiwan.

•	Built in 1952, it’s designed like a traditional Chinese palace with a red exterior, golden roof tiles, and intricate carvings.
•	The grand lobby and hallways feel like stepping into a piece of history.

The hotel has multiple restaurants serving authentic Chinese, Cantonese, and Sichuan cuisine, along with Western options.
•	The dim sum and Peking duck are especially famous.

The hotel has hosted world leaders, celebrities, and dignitaries for decades. Staying here feels like being part of history.
•	The interior features dragon pillars, golden ceilings, and antique art pieces that showcase Taiwan’s cultural pride.

Perched on Yuanshan Hill, it offers panoramic views of Taipei.
•	At night, the illuminated building itself becomes one of Taipei’s landmarks, visible from across the city.

Even if you don’t stay overnight, many visitors come just to tour the lobby, dine, or take photos.
•	It’s a blend of luxury, tradition, and history in one spot.

My parents were visiting from the UK, so I decided to treat them for their wedding anniversary! They loved it !!!! They had an amazing stay! They loved the architectural style and the history of the building. Also the free bus to Yuanshan station was great!!! The staff were very friendly and courteous and they loved the breakfast! Super beautiful!!! Thank you so much for making my parents vacation special! No other hotel could compare ! They will definitely be back next time !

If you love vintage vibes, it might be okay for you, but not for me. 😆 The breakfast and dinner buffets were nice, but not very varied in food choices. reviews.text:
Fun Inn Taipei has its pros and cons. The location is excellent—very convenient for getting around the city. The staff and host are great, always responsive and helpful, which really made the stay easier. The beds are also comfortable, which is a big plus.

That said, the building itself is quite run down, not very well maintained, and cleanliness could be improved. Common areas and facilities didn’t feel very fresh. Overall, it’s fine for a short stay if you value location, friendly staff, and a decent bed, but don’t expect a spotless or modern environment.

It’s alright, nothing amazing. I stayed in a 6 bed dorm and the room was very cramped, the lockers can touch the door to exit. There is a en-suite bathroom and shower which is decent. The weekday rates are reasonable but what’s nuts is the weekend price, on booking.com for Saturday it’s $52 USD What a joke. The other days it’s $12-$15 USD which is very fair rate. So for weekend I would just avoid it in general. The lockers are good, the mattress is good, just the room is very very tight. Common area is ok. This is the type of place If you’re the type of traveler who needs a place to sleep and shower and that’s all. Location is good wifi is good

The only good thing about this hostel is the location. They “clean” the room but it’s not really clean — vacuumed for like 30 seconds and the trash in the dorm room wasn’t emptied for days.  We arrived on October 1 and left on October 4, and the trash on the common desk was still piled up.
The bed is super uncomfortable, you can feel the springs. It’s also self-service, so you have to remove your own sheets when checkout

The beds are ok, quite comfortable actually. The problem is that there is just one toilet and shower for too many people, no control on respecting the silence at night, so people where talking laud, making noises, Turing on light even in the middle of the night. No good communication about the common area in the basement, we sorted on the floor while waiting for the check-in time and they even ask us to move to not be in the middle (even if there was no one that we were bothering) without telling us that there was a common area with sofa and chairs.

The hostel was descent clean, had good enough beds, functioning in all the essential ways an affordable hostel needs to -- except for the wifi. I travel. A lot. There is no reason or excuse for stays to have poor wifi (especially in a city).

With no exaggeration it took well over 15 mins just to load the google results to get to share this review. Quite ridiculous if you ask me.

We really enjoyed our stay here! The hotel is a bit older but still really nice. The hot spring tub in the room was the highlight of our stay- we used it multiple times per day and it was very luxurious and easily fit two people.

The location is up a hill but in a perfect location to see all that Beitou has to offer. Would 100% suggest this place for a relaxing hot spring stay at an affordable price!

Grand Pleasure Spring Hotel is a wonderful place to stay. The staff are very kind and welcoming, and the atmosphere is peaceful from the moment you arrive. The rooms are clean and comfortable with relaxing hot spring baths. The surrounding scenery is beautiful, with green hills and fresh air that make it easy to unwind. A perfect spot in Beitou to relax and enjoy both comfort and nature.

We recently stayed at this hot spring hotel, and it was truly one of the most relaxing experiences we've ever had. From the moment we arrived, the atmosphere was peaceful and welcoming. The natural hot springs were absolutely amazing—clean, soothing, and perfectly maintained. We spent hours just soaking and unwinding.

The staff was incredibly friendly and attentive, always making sure we had everything we needed. Our room was spotless, comfortable, and offered a beautiful view. Every detail, from the cozy bedding to the tranquil surroundings, helped us fully disconnect and recharge.

We can’t recommend this place enough for anyone looking to escape the stress of daily life. Already planning our next visit!

My first time in Taiwan and this place is my first hotel in Taiwan too, everything look so quiet about this area and I like it, the staff so nice. But I don’t know my room don’t have windows lol and I cannot do anything with air conditioning (they turn on it but no remote to control haha) so it so hot at my time about room at second floor. But everything look so good about this place especially the bath 🤩

Such a charming place nestled a little higher up from the city center. Accommodating staff, spacious rooms (they had a charming old-timey feel to them), and excellent bath. Sadly, no restaurant, but they did have a limited menu for room service. We commuted to Xinbeitou from Ximen with our luggage in tow, the walk from the bus stop to the hotel would have been fine, but it was all uphill. I was sweat drenched and panting like a horse by the time we got there, but it just meant that getting in the bath was the perfect opportunity to rest my aching muscles.

reviews.text:
Perfect location with perfect room!

Has been a very enjoyable stay. The ac is strong, bed is huge and comfortable and clean, water heater is hot with a nice clean Japanese WC and bathtub.
Service is done very well every day.
Location is very convenient along the red, green and yellow line. Close to the Taipei Main Station.
Full stars given. Totally enjoyed our 6 days stay in the hotel!

This hotel was amazing in some ways, and left a bit to be desired in other ways.

The positives: It was fairly quiet in the sense that I barely saw any other guests the entire time we were there -- a whole week. Also, our room and bed were both MASSIVE! This was very welcomed after several weeks of tiny rooms in Japan and then moving on to more tiny rooms in South Korea. The air conditioning worked well. And finally, the free laundry was absolutely amazing.

The negatives: While we didn't see anyone else, the walls were REALLY thin to where you could hear conversations, people throwing up, people having sex, etc. The mini fridge in our room was on but wasn't cold at all so our food we bought the first night spoiled. And the holder for the shower head was broken to where if you put too much water pressure, the water would spray all over, but then when you would turn it off, the shower head would loudly fall to the ground.

Loved the room we got. Was facing the main road and had a nice rustic view. Checking in was quick and the room was spacious. Exceedingly clean and comfortable. We got a huge king size bed and a big bathroom for what we paid for. Its location is also very central and between 3 different mrt lines. We enjoyed our stay in this hotel and would definitely book it again when we come back to Taiwan.

I recommend this place. It's near the Zhongshan metro, and there's a Family Mart right below. Super big bathroom with a separate bathtub and shower along with a toilet that has a Japanese automated bidet. The only set back is that the WiFi was a bit unstable. I ended up using my hopspot for data stability and consistency.

It's clean i guess. But the shower didn't work properly (the shower head mount was broken... so i had to take a bath...) and the wifi was not very fast. Otherwise it was fine for the price. Good enough for two nights.

reviews.text: Compared to the price, the amazing condition of the room, location, and the service of the staff were very friendly. Thank you for keeping the luggage even after the check-out and for the convenience of the guest despite the inconvenient request. Overall, it left a clean and kind impression.

This is a lovely, clean hotel in an excellent location, close to buses, metro and trains and with plenty of food options around. I had a very comfortable stay and returned later to stay here again. The staff are especially friendly and helpful with everything. The room rate was good value too! I recommend staying here and I hope to stay again soon.

Stayed here for 14 days on extended business trip to Taipei. The hotel is quite close to Taipei Main Station, only a 15 minute walk, so it is convenient to get to from Taoyuan Airport taking the Airport Express. The hotel itself is not big, but it is well run and clean. The staff speaks English and are quite helpful if you have questions. There is always staff at the front desk to help. The downstairs lobby of hotel has some room to work and free coffee, tea, and snacks. The rooms will be small, but acceptable for the price. I chose the Standard room, so it is the smallest, but there are bigger rooms available. Despite the size and no windows, the room was decent with a comfortable, desk, small fridge, hot water kettle, safe, and plenty of lights and power sockets. The bathroom is typical of these hotels with an open shower next to toilet and sink. No issues with that and the water pressure and temperature were fine. I like to use washcloths, that they did not provide, but I had my own. Wi-Fi was free and reasonably fast. The rooms were cleaned regularly and tea/coffee/water replenished. I had no issues with noise. The hotel is located in the Linsen St area, which has lots of bars and clubs, but I did not hear any noise, but rooms facing street might. The area is safe, has lots of great restaurants, especially Japanese ramen and izakaya places, and is close to MRT and Youbike stations. Will definitely return again, this place is friendly, clean, and a good deal.

Room is clean and comfortable. Staff is friendly and helpful. Location wise is good as well with a variety of local street food. We are truly grateful with the staff’s assistance and finding our misplaced ring. Would definitely recommend!
Rooms are clean and front desk receptionist are exceptionally friendly and approachable. Highly recommend!
