reviews.text:
I had to change rooms once due to different booking so I tried both window (superior) and non window (standard) room.

For standard room, there is window in the non window room but the window just can't open. Room is relatively smaller than superior room but it is still wide and spacious. The room I got was next to the water refill machine and the staff exit so it can get a bit loud if the staff slams the door but it didn't affect me.

For superior room, you can open the window and there is a balcony. Depending where your room faces, the sun can get really bright but black out curtains do the trick just well. On certain floors there are complementary snacks and drinks but not all. There was a bath tub in my room.

Pros:
- This hotel has good facilities, is modern, good service and very clean
- There was sale when I booked and the price didn't increase much when I checked same day booking
- The hotel is directly in front of Love Pier which was great for walking and sight seeing. There was a weekend market when I was there.
- Light rail within 5mins walk
- For female lone travellers, I would recommend this hotel if you don't mind traveling a bit far from the city.

Cons:
- Far from city center, takes 30mins by public transport to go to city center
- There is a Ok Mart downstairs but options are little
- For a hotel so good, I was surprised the breakfast was just soso

Really loved everything about this place. The location is super convenient, just a short walk to Pier 2 and the light rail which makes getting around so easy. The price is great for what you get. The room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and the overall vibe was nice. It feels modern yet cozy and the staff were friendly and helpful. Everything felt reasonable. I had a very good stay and slept really well. My room even had a nice view of the music hall which was a lovely bonus.

We traveled all over Taiwan and this was by far our worst hotel experience. We arrived late. Our room smelled of cigarette smoke. The hallway was also smelly — tobacco, mildew, stale food. We went down to the lobby, where a grumpy receptionist, visibly annoyed to be disturbed, curtly agreed to change our rooms. He moved us to another room on the same floor which was much smaller — we barely had enough space to put our suitcases. We were traveling with our friends, whose room was initially fine, but they too were woken up at 6am by a smell of cigarettes, and were told to pack and bring their suitcases down to the lobby if they wanted to change rooms. The odor was everywhere. The next day we asked for a partial refund to compensate for our small room, but the receptionists said the rate was the same for all rooms. Don't come here — the hotel smells and feels like a depressed old man's breath.

It is a really nice experience that I live in City Suites. This is my second time that I choose City Suits. All of their hotels have a really good location, excellent services and nice room design. I think if you come to Kaohsiung or say Taiwan, it is a good choice for your comfortable trip.

Good points
- vibes and design
- location

Bad points
- customer service
- air conditioning
- mosquito proof
- toilet smell design

The air conditioning is 27 degrees permanently even when the temperature is set to 20 degrees. Only one of the 3 air conditioning vent is blowing air. Called customer service and a old man came up to check. Started with very poor attitude, saying there is nothing he can do about it, blaming us for not informing earlier when checked in. Followed with saying that the control to change temperature does not work, it’s just for display. I have another pair of friend that verified the control to change temperature works in another room, so the old man was lying to us. He offered to change the room, but we have our luggages unpacked so we asked if we can sleep in another room for the night while leaving the luggages there (it’s the last night). He declined and said there is nothing he can do. I suggested the air conditioning should be reviewed and improved, he just said there is nothing to be done. To add on, not a single apology was mentioned for the poor attitude and the poor room service. Sleeping without blanket was tough too since there was mosquito in the room on the first night. The toilet room for the toilet bowl has a huge gap on top of the door, poop smell will reek into the room when used. Overall quite an unpleasant experience, only plus point is that it looks nice.

When asking to change coin for the laundry room, to use the washing machine, the respond was unfriendly as well.

reviews.text:
Booked this hotel because of its strategic location where you are next to Bo Er and light rail in front, plus walking distance to many attractions.

We did a casual room tour video which you can refer as we booked for 3 queen beds room for a family stay.
Overall the interior is well maintained (likely because it's new), and the amenities are satisfying.

Only the services from the night shift front desk was kinda let down during our stay, otherwise it would be 5 ⭐.

The hotel is in a very convenient location, just right opposite 駁二蓬萊站, and you can easily rent a scooter or use uBike nearby.
We stayed for 2 nights (~HKD $1788) — honestly felt a bit overpriced for what we got. The room has a smart TV with Netflix and YouTube, and the bed was comfy and nice to sleep on.

You can do online check-in, and they’ll send you a door password — remember to screenshot it. There are some free drinks provided too, which is a nice touch.

But some downsides:

The faucet and shower head had noticeable water stains, and the water pressure wasn’t great.
The curtains don’t block light well, so it gets quite bright in the morning.
Overall, decent stay but not value for money — good location but the room details could be better.

Staying at this hotel was a wonderful experience! The staff was great and the rooms were clean and smelled great and the environment was wonderful to be in. The location is super convenient for getting around the city and near everything you wanna be near. Bonus, there were snacks and water for free in the lobby and they were delicious. they also had umbrellas for rainy days and right next to Pier two for when you don’t feel like going far. I highly recommend anyone who’s thinking about traveling to Koasiung to stay at the Papo’a Harbor Hotel!

Great location. Steps from LRT green line. Walk to everything. Our room walls could use a coat of paint however the room was very clean. Good free internet. The MOST comfortable bed and sheets I've ever slept in. Helpful friendly staff helped me with on line check in and obtaining key codes without a Taiwan cell number. Good value. Will absolutely stay here again next time we visit. Thanks for a nice stay.
Really nice hotel. The staff and especially the manager at the time was super helpful and nice. Would definitely come back again.

reviews.text:
This hotel shares space with local residents. It's located on the 12th floor. There is no actual lobby on the ground floor. Walk through the food stores to get to the building entrance.
Great location with lots of food and public transport.
The hotel offers 100twd for a load of laundry wash. Great and helpful staff.

The room is comfortable, the staff is friendly and helpful. We arrived there early, before the check in time, but she allowed us to place our luggage in the room first. She also guided us where to buy things.

The location is great, plenty of food choices, the night market is right at the street outside the hotel entrance, there are 7 eleven and family mart outside the hotel. The nearest MRT station is just 3-5mins walk away. Very convenient.

Nice budget hotel located in the heart of the city. Close to every: metro, shopping, market, coffee, Starbucks etc
Rooms are a little old but you got everything you need for a short stay.

Love the interior, every rooms takes on a train station, super cute! Staff are very helpful and friendly, breakfast is provided, very affordable,  hotel room is neat, there's a comfy bed, a scenic view from the balcony what more can you ask for?

Living within a food market. Our dream.
Clean, spacious and kind staff. Recommended.

reviews.text:
Family Trip for 4.

Impromptu booking after we decided to street stay in kaoshiung an extra night and the airbnb we were staying opposite, couldn't extend an extra night.

Reviews were complaining about a smell.. so I walked in but it was much better than the online complaints and I booked straight away.

Rooms are all new, power points are all international so you don't need adapters and there's even a water dispenser in the bathroom!  Bed is massive and clean. 5 stars for only 4876twd for 2 rooms! Location 5 stars. Right around the corner to Liuhe Night Market downstairs. And 3-5 minutes walk to MRT.

I have stayed in many places across Taiwan. Would say this is the best value hotel I stayed during trip. Friendly staff and also offer laundry services. Breakfast is provided. Very clean room and quite spacious. Very near the MRT and night market. Would stay here again.

Stayed here for 2 nights while on a trip to Kaohsiung with my friend and had a good experience!
Pros:
- super convenient location, right next to the Formosa Boulevard station (transfer station between the Orange and Red MRT lines)
- clean, well-equipped, and new rooms! The beds were comfy, there was ample closet space, and even the bathroom was spacious
- friendly and helpful staff!

Cons:
- the lobby and hallway had a distinct smell that’s hard to describe but strange. My friend and I couldn’t really tell what it was?
- the room has a faint cigarette smell, but it’s not a huge bother as I only noticed it when I walked in.

Overall, convenient location and clean rooms! Would recommend :)

It’s a very nice room though it’s small and has no window. There is good technology and lighting in the room - buttons for lights. For the bed - it’s acceptable and the breakfast is thorough. The reason for the low rating is just that there is a weird vibe about the place. There is no friendliness with the front desk stuff And they both act and appear very offputting. Horror movie vibes. There’s no electrical outlet by the bed, which is bonkers.

Travelling in a group of 4 so we booked 2 rooms. Upon check in, the receptionist said that one of the room has been upgraded due to overbooking, which was a pleasant surprise. However, the air conditioning in the upgraded room turned out to be a nightmare. The thermostat was set to 23 (lowest) and after a whole afternoon, the room cooled down to 25 when nobody was inside. After we entered the room, it remained at 26 and we were sweating while sitting in the room. After our feedback to the reception, they came to ‘unlock’ the min temp to 18 but the room temperature did not go down. We requested to downgrade back to the room type we’ve booked, thinking that it’s due to the large size of the room that cause the air conditioning to be not cold. We were told that there’re no extra rooms and then also discovered that 80% of the air con vent was blocked with only a tiny breeze. After several calls to the reception, they said that there’s a room available and we had to wait an hour to change the room and it was already past midnight. The corridor leading to the rooms was also non air conditioned and air was stale.
The location of the hotel is great but would not recommend for stay during summer.

By the way, the rooms either had a curtain that opens up to a wall (no window) or has windows that opens up to the wall of the opposite building …

reviews.text: Decent hotel in a convenient location not in the city center but close to the Weiwuying Park which has a lot of offerings and a very short walk from the MRT which gets you to the city Center in 10 minutes. The only issue I had was the balcony door didn’t fully seal so a lot of street noise bled through. However if you turn the fan up all the way it’s enough to drown out the noise so I had no issues sleeping. Breakfast is decent, not the absolute best I’ve had but they also serve complimentary snacks and fresh made waffles and popcorn in the afternoon which is pretty rare. Would stay here again.

Room, location and staff service was ok and as expected for a 3 star hotel. Breakfast was quite mediocre.

Stay was really average but the worst is the horrible wifi speed which is pretty much a crime nowadays.

If you need good wifi stay, do not stay in this hotel.
It was just a 3 minute walk from the MRT. We were able to navigate easily. The bed was great. Rooms and bathrooms were spotless. Breakfast was included and was authentic.

We stayed at a family room (can fit up to 5 members) and we had a really good experience. The room was spacious and had everything we needed. The aircon system was superb as well.
Location-wise, there’s a subway station 3 minutes away by foot. Nearby, theres a Mos burger thats opened up to 24h.
Breakfast is included and the food was decent:)!
Very comfortable bed with laundry (free wash, $10 dry for 10 mins), gym room, breakfast and afternoon tea. Also close to the mrt station. I had a comfortable stay and highly recommend!

reviews.text: Honestly one of the best places I've stayed, great price, great location, great amenities and service. It's right next to the bus stop which goes directly to Kaohsiung Main Station and next to a very busy and yummy duck rice eatery. It's also an 8 minute walk from Yangchengpu Station and very close to the Pier 2 Art Gallery. The host is also a great guy, speaks fluent English and always up for a good chat. Will be back again next time I'm in the hood

Stayed here on 13-15 Sep 2024. Very good location if you only have few days to explore Kaohsiung, since all mainstream tourist must visit is on the district. Also have many nice restaurants nearby. Just accross 7Eleven.

Due to the budget we stayed on the smallest room. But it was OK for us. Self check in is very easy. Property is quite new, English-speaking host, have good interior design, free coffee on the lobby.

Little minus: Soundproof issue. If another guests pass-by in the middle of the night, you can hear their steps and sounds.

I recently stayed at Ox Suites in the Yancheng district of Kaohsiung, and it was an exceptional experience. Ron and his wife run a fantastic little block of serviced apartments that’s clean, modern, and minimalist, yet equipped with everything you might need—and more. The apartment was spotless, and the minimalist design made it feel spacious and comfortable.

Ron went above and beyond by providing a comprehensive list of things to do in the Yancheng area, which was incredibly helpful. If you only have three nights, like I did, you’ll find plenty to keep you busy just in Yancheng and nearby Cijin. Their recommendations were spot on, and they were always just a message away if I needed anything or had any questions.

The location is also a major plus. It’s just a short walk to Yancheng station on the orange line, making it easy to get around. You can easily reach the hotel with just one change of train line from the HSR Station.

Overall, I had a fantastic stay and will definitely be back the next time I’m in Kaohsiung. Highly recommended!

From requesting about the booking to the end of our stay, the owner Ron has been super friendly and helpful to any of our questions. We arrived early on the day about 1pm, although the checkin time is 4pm, Ron told us they had the room done and could let us in straight away! It was a very nice surprise! We stayed in room 603, it was very clean and comfortable. The shower was responsive to the temperature very well with a great pressure. The mattress was not too hard and not too soft which I like. Even though the building is located right on a main road, it was really quiet and peaceful during our whole stay. We had a very enjoyable time! Thank you 😊

I'd give this place six stars if I could:

- Modern rooms with TVs, cold AC and powerful water pressure (as well as Smart Toilets).
- Reverse osmosis systems for pure water.
- The downstairs has a shared lobby with drinks fridge, snacks and free coffee and laundry facilities.
- The owner speaks English and is happy to give tips for places to visit, where to eat etc.
- The location has you within easy walking distance of the pier arts centre, alien art gallery, international convention centre and everything you could need to survive like markets and food.
- Bus stop outside which doubles as a very convenient uber/taxi pull-up spot.
- 7/11 across the road which has an ATM.

We only stayed 1 night and left really early in the morning.

Good location, big bed and room size with no wondow. When I booked through Agoda, it's for 3 days but when checkin - they claimed that 1st night is 3 hours. The blonde hair colour receptionist was not friendly, told me I had to move out after 3 hrs! Ended I had to pay more even with Agoda booking! Toilet shower should have a blind to stop the water from splashing all over the sink n wet my toiletries.

Location is a few steps walk from Famosa Boulevard mrt, convenient.
This hotel place is perfect, near MRT station and night market. Cheap price also for the room rates and the room is clean also the toilet is perfect! I recommend this when you visit Kaoshiung
Affordable accommodation and friendly staffs. Location is near the MRT station and night market. Definitely I will recommend to travellers to book and stay.

I had a great stay at this hotel! The service was excellent and very professional. I checked in at 3 PM and everything went smoothly. The room was super clean, the air conditioning was icy cold, and the Wi-Fi was incredibly fast. Plus, the hotel is right next to the BTS station, which made getting around the city really convenient. Highly recommended!

reviews.text:
Room decor was lovely, furniture comfortable,  amenities convenient to use, breakfast was tasty, and it is very good for even lacto-vegetarians. Staff was very well-informed and gracefully friendly. Staff can communicate well in English, as well.
Location is very near to Gushan Ferry point, about 20 min walk. Very convenient to get to any public transport, as well.

Location was superb—walking distance to Pier 2 Art Center and Liouhe night market. I did have a bad time interacting with the staff, who were overwhelmingly rude. The customer service overall was terrible. They won’t even let you get a cup of coffee in the lobby until 10am unless you buy a breakfast voucher, which isn’t worth it; you can get better breakfast from the plethora of little restaurants in the area. The room was clean, but the “view” is a tiny window about five feet above the ground so it’s hard to see unless you stand on the couch, the fridge doesn’t work, and there are three sets of light switches so it’s a guessing game to figure out how to turn specific lights on or off. Overall acceptable but wouldn’t stay here again.

Very good hotel. My family room had free instant noodles. Room is generally very clean and hotel is not too far from station but is a problem to bring the luggage there. The breakfast there is very good. Based on the day you live there, you can get fries and nuggets or others like spaghetti. Overall for me a 5 out of 5
this is the first hotel I slept 6 hours straight on my first night. bed is soft and comfortable. Stay here for 3 nights.  🫶
I really like this 🏨 hotel,close to public transportation and very friendly 😊 service. I even got a little gift 🎁. How sweet!

reviews.text: No frills hotel! I’ve stayed here a couple of times now when visiting Kaohsiung. It’s a pretty decent hotel, basic, simple and clean. I’ve always had assistance when checking in which was a good thing because the second time, something went wrong and staff were able to assist me and correct the error that the self check in machine caused. I like the fact that they have a room that accommodates 3 people. We got that room and it was spacious. The bathtub is pretty cool. Last time we didn’t have a shower curtain and water went everywhere so I asked for one and the next day we got it. Location is good too!

The room has quite a few steps, and I've found myself tripping over them. This may not be the most accessible option for elderly guests. However, aside from that issue, I have no other complaints about the hotel. They offered amenities like washing machines, a dryer, and a 24-hour friendly front desk. The location is excellent—quiet and very well-maintained. If I return to Kaohsiung, this hotel will definitely be my top choice.

P.S.: If you or your children become ill, there’s a clinic and pharmacy nearby where you can receive treatment.

After paying for the room they decided the booking was 'fraudulent', so I cancelled it and now they are saying they do not have my money and they are not giving me a refund. I have raised the issue with Booking.com. Some people call that stealing.

The location and the helpful staff members are the best things about this place. The lobby is by far nicer than the rest of the hotel. As a previous commenter mentioned, the rooms don't always feel the cleanest. Surfaces such as the desk and bedside tables had streaks and ring marks left behind by god knows what, and the sink also had some mysterious brown stains on the outer surface. The bathroom had a sour smell, and the overall room had a mustiness. The AC is also barely functional, as is the fridge. I also found there were some tears in the mattress bedding and found strands of hair on the bed and scattered throughout the floor. The leather-like chair also did not seem very clean, with some parts of the chair being a noticeably darker colour than others. The rooms also don't have the best soundproofing. From the hallway, you can hear if one of your neighbours is using the shower. I was also woken up by a neighbor leaving their room, and they weren't even loud - all they did was let their door fall shut.

There is also one water refilling station and a washing machine + dryer on the main floor, past the check-in counter. Both are free for guests to use, but the washer and dryer have seen better days, and you will need to source your own detergent.

The staff member that greeted us was very nice, however. She walked us through what was available at the hotel and also answered our questions with a lot of patience.

Location is close to shinkuchan, which has a pretty diverse collection of shops, including phone accessories, hair salons and tattoo parlours, and a good selection of nice little restaurants and bars.

Overall, I would not stay here again unless a lot of things changed.

The self-check in was a breeze. I was a bit worried about that because I had read complaints of that aspect of Guide hotels in Taipei. We went to drop off our luggage before our rooms were ready and luckily, there was still front staff to help us. We asked for bottles of water which they were fine with giving us.

The room was huge. There is both a standing shower with 6 interesting jets and a bathtub with its own shower head. The beds were big. The only fault I can find is the AC was a bit cranky. For the price range, I think the rooms are definitely 5-star. I have definitely stayed at hotels that are 4x the price that had worse facilities.

The location is very convenient. Lots of great cafes, restaurants nearby, close to the ShinJuKu shopping area and the MRT.

We left our luggage in the lobby again the day we departed and picked it up pretty late at night with no problem.

reviews.text:
After 10 PM, the entire mall becomes deserted and dark, creating an incredibly exhilarating and unique atmosphere for an evening stroll – truly an unforgettable experience! The view over the harbor is simply incredible, making waking up a genuine pleasure.
The staff were exceptionally friendly, helpful, and accommodating from the moment I checked in. They provided excellent support, explained everything clearly, and even gave a thoughtful goodbye gift. Complimentary water was a nice touch, and the entire place, including the shared bathrooms, was spotlessly clean. There were always enough shower cabins available, and you also have access to the shopping center's restrooms.
My only minor critique would be that the air conditioning units could use a cleaning. Given the compact size of the rooms, the stale smell from the AC was unfortunately more noticeable. Also, while the "boxes" (rooms) are perfectly adequate for most luggage, do keep in mind that you won't have space to spread out very large suitcases.
A useful tip: if you plan on checking in after 10 PM, be sure to notify them in advance, otherwise you might not be able to get in. Overall, KW2 offers a distinct and highly recommendable stay for those seeking something a bit out of the ordinary.

I loved it. February 2024. I paid 2000 NT for two nights, the idea is good, having to tap everywhere is kind of a bothersome and also, during the day the shops clients are a little bit too close to the hostel... However, I'm trying to book now march 2025 and the price is more than double 😱 kind of a shame.

You need a key to take a piss. You have  to swipe your card in and out. Annoying. And it's quite loud during the day as you are literally living in a mall. Most of the toilets are closed at night?????????????? Only one entrance to the establishment late night. Intricate door lock system to follow. The jazz music they play nonstop is awful no offense.

The check in process is a bit of a nuisance. They insist on you using a kiosk, but a person needs to help you do every step which seems superfluous. At night when people are trying to do self check in using the kiosk it is super annoying as the automated voice keeps talking and it disturbs those in the cabins near the kiosk. People trying to check in ended up having to make a phone call. There is a room full of showers and sinks which is clean and only accessible to the hostel guests, however the toilets are accessible to the public, and they aren't as clean or private. Lastly the security gates to and from the hostel private area are difficult to open and close so they were often left ajar, therefore making things less secure. During the day I saw tourists wanting to check out the hostel cabins so security could be a bit at risk. The cabins/rooms were quite nice and comfortable, very simple and seemed clean. Don't bet on being able to sleep in past ten AM because that's when the mall just below the hostel (hostel is on a loft) opens and there's quite a bit of noise. Location wise it is awesome and you have access to tons of food, sites, and conveniences. The rooms all have AC units. Because they are small, you may not be able to keep your luggage open inside the room. The rooms unfortunately do not have many hooks, there were only two in our room which is not enough.

The best location in Kaohsiung! You can sleep right at Pier 2. Check-in is automated, but we had assistance from the helpful staff member (it may be more tricky if you arrive very late). The gates to exit/enter are troublesome at first. You must push the gates slightly before pulling them open (then it becomes easy). This is a concept hostel in partnership with Muji. I stayed Fri night. I am only surprised that the place is not full of people. Occupancy is low for some reason.

Stayed at Inns Hotel for a couple of nights during my trip to Kaohsiung. The location is very convenient — close to metro stations, and just a short walk to Liuhe Night Market, which was great for grabbing a quick bite for supper.

Not my first stay, stayed 2023 too :)

If you are a light sleeper please don’t stay here. The soundproofing is terrible, you can hear everything from the hallway. Especially if you stay on a floor with a water dispenser you will keep hearing people in the hallway running back and forward. Even if people use the toilet or shower you can hear them. And when people are walking upstairs you can hear it too.

Too bad the hotel itself is great, very convenient and the staff are so nice and welcoming. If you are not affected by noise then definitely stay here. But if you are a light sleeper I suggest you stay clear.

A standard hotel but it has a luxurious feel to it. Rooms have all the basics (fridge, kettle, Aircon) and a decent size bathroom. The coffee machine downstairs is a nice touch. Location is ok and quiet at night. 15min walk to the MRT.

Clean rooms, great service and free coffee and tea in the lobby. Located near some great bars, convenience stores and breakfast shops as well as the Liuhe Night Market.

Environmentally conscious as well as they offer water coolers on every floor and large refillable shampoo, body wash and conditioner in the toilet.

reviews.text: The service staff's attitude is really 100 points, especially the white-haired gentleman who is thoughtful and polite, making people feel very courteous; as for the cleanliness of the room, it needs to be improved. Several parts are dirty, which is a pity for such an elegant and comfortable decoration!

The soundproofing in the room was really poor. The music from upstairs was loud and the occasional clatter of high heels made it difficult to sleep. The room wasn't cleaned very thoroughly either. There were a lot of hairs hanging from the bathroom drain, which was a real sight. Although the room was non-smoking, the smell of cigarette smoke wafted into the room all night, and it was even stronger when the door was opened.

Let me be frank.

The staff were very friendly, providing extra cookies and bottled water. The room was clean and reasonably tidy, and the decor was quite new.

However, if you need a quiet hotel in the middle of the night, and you're staying below a noisy hotel, you're bound to have a restful night.

The constant clatter of bass speakers and high heels from upstairs, and the constant clatter of traffic on the street outside—even earplugs couldn't block it out.

Although I was able to change rooms after reporting the situation to the hotel staff at 4:00 AM, the entire floor above is occupied by a hotel, so the noise was still quite loud.

If you ignore the noise, the Muchen Hotel in downtown Kaohsiung offers excellent value for money. It's a shame.

Let's start with the good parts: the environment is relatively new, clean, the water pressure and temperature are acceptable, and the front desk service is friendly.

The bad part is the obvious lack of soundproofing. Even though I requested a quiet room, the neighbors started partying in the early hours, and the singing was completely piercing (and damn, it was awful). The sound of footsteps from upstairs and the clatter of traffic all night long was also clearly heard. And let's not even talk about the TV remote being laggy.

I just saw the Google reviews now. If I had known it would be so noisy, I wouldn't have stayed there. Don't even mention promises of improvements. Someone already reported the soundproofing issue a month ago. Consider moving or closing down.

The new decoration feels very good, the environment is comfortable, you can temporarily store your luggage, and there are counter staff. However, the floor is downstairs of the hotel. There will be the sound of high heels and KTV singing in the middle of the night. Light sleepers need to wear earplugs. The sound will not stop until about 4 o'clock.
When flushing the toilet, you need to close the drain hole of the sink, otherwise the smell will be discharged!
The hair dryer is fixed on the wall, which is not very easy to use. The shower gel is slippery. For those who are very concerned about this, it is better to bring your own. There is a lot of storage space, the room is large, and the price is quite reasonable. There is no parking space for motorcycles. You need to park in the surrounding parks.
The bathroom is separated from wet and dry, there are no small towels, they are disposable ones

reviews.text:
This place was booked by accident and had non-refundable policy through Booking.com. We needed to cancel and the staff went above and beyond to make sure we got a full refund.

For this reason, if and when we visit Kaohsiung in the future, we'll definitely be staying here to show our gratitude.

Thank you!

Great location, but poor cleanliness

The location is super convenient, but the place feels more like an Airbnb than a proper hotel. Cleanliness was lacking — lint in the hairdryer, dusty corners, and an old futon with visible stains that clearly hadn’t been cleaned.

The welcome guide had a passive-aggressive tone, basically saying that if you don’t report issues during your stay — especially related to cleanliness — then it’s your own fault for not having a good experience. It felt like they were shifting the responsibility of cleanliness onto the customer, which is not what you’d expect from any place that calls itself a hotel.

If you are planning to stay the night just for the convenience, yes.
If you are staying w family, pay another $200 go to a proper hotel that’s a stone throw away.

Really nice clean rooms, excellent location right by the night market and Formosa street, and very friendly accommodating staff. When I had to cancel my last night due to a family emergency they really helped me out even when booking.com would not. 10/10 recommend and thank you very much!!

The best "budget" hotel I've ever stayed in. Location is great, right next to the night market and a few minutes walk from the metro. Our rooms was very spacious and spotless. Highly recommend this hotel for anyone staying in Kaohsiung.

The check-in process was easy and smooth, the staff members were very responsive on social (LINE). The location was perfect and the room was specious and clean. They even helped me glued my luggage tag, so kind! Will definitely stay there again when I visit Kaohsiung next time :)

reviews.text: The staff was absolutely wonderful and went above and beyond to accommodate us by matching the price we found in Bogotá, which we truly appreciated. They gave us a beautiful room with a stunning river view, and the space was both spacious and very comfortable. The bathtub was amazing and made our stay even more relaxing. The hotel offers a nice concept with a beautiful harbor view. I loved the bathroom. The breakfast buffet was pretty average, and the staff was honestly not that friendly- they seemed annoyed by any requests or questions. There are also children everywhere running, laughing, screaming & crying. This property is great for a family, but as a solo traveler, I can’t recommend it.
Excellent stay in Kaohsiung! Great value for money, very good service, and a beautiful room with parking included. The location near Pier-2 is perfect — ideal place to stay when visiting the city!

A humble clean hotel albeit in a relatively distant location from the main city.

The staff were kind and very accommodating. The rooms were large and the property offered complimentary breakfast buffet. We were delighted to see that they change dishes by the hour depending on what choices are eaten up!

Overall this was extremely attractive considering the price for one night is

Reading other reviews, I understand what guests have said about the smell in the lobby and outside floor level elevators. It smells musty and like sewer. I’m not sure if that within the hotel’s control? The room definitively did not have the same smell. We had a fabulous view of the river, which is beautiful during the day and exceptional at night with all the lights. The room was spacious and well-equipped. My only issue with the room was the central air conditioning was set to a very cold temperature. Leaving it on was much too cold, and turning it off was much too warm, and then muggy. We really loved the room regardless and the location was amazing. Proximity to the pier to walk around and take the ferry to Cijin was great, plus a walk up and down the river was lovely. Lots of spots to get food, night markets, and walk to metro stations as well. We consider a great location 15-30 min walk to the things we like or need. Front desk staff was kind and efficient, allowing us to check in early as well as store our bags after check out. I would stay here again for location alone, but the buffet breakfast was not good. Skip it - there are some great local spots within 5-10 min walk for a fraction of the cost and better quality.

reviews.text: The room is compact, almost tight, but it's well designed and there is a decently done full bath that's finished with quality material. I would stay here again except almost no buses run on this avenue, not sure why, it's a major thoroughfare. The MRT stop is a good hike away

The hotel stands strikingly in the centre of Kaoshiung city. You can tell that it is recently built or renovated. Exterior and interior is well designed and comfortable. They have an open self serve facilities on the ground floor for free coffee/tea bad snacks. Staff are friendly, professional and are willing to help for any additional accessories you need. For a double bed room is at a competitive price, considering it is only a 5min walk from the central MRT station and 15min walk from the nearest night market.
However there is two things that prevent me from giving this place full marks. The use of "packets" for shampoo, conditioner and body wash gel. Of course this is only a minor problem considering how beautiful, modern and well maintained bathroom they have. However there is a fatal flaw in the bathroom, or I should say "wetroom"? A flimsy curtain separate the shower area from the toilet and sink. This curtain does nothing. Within minutes your entire bathroom floor wet. If they had just installed a physical barrier next to the toilet or at least stop the water from flooding (putting a wet towel on the floor will help). However this atrocious flaw is compounded by having no shelves to put any of your bathroom necessities on. If you have only the "packets" that are given, you will end up putting the spent packages on the toilet.
If it is a short stay, room cleaning will help having these flaws annoy you. But if you are one who do not like using room cleaning often or worried about privacy (rooms have no safes either) these bathroom flaws will became apparent and depending on your tolerances, can be a turn off.
It is a shame, because I ultimately enjoyed my stay here but the bathroom flaw got worse the longer you stay.

Lagom is a Swedish word and cultural concept that embodies the idea of "just the right amount" – not too much, not too little. It signifies a philosophy of moderation, balance, and finding harmony in all aspects of life, promoting sustainability, social awareness, and contentment with what is sufficient rather than always striving for more

Péssima experiência no Mu-in Hotel Kaohsiung / Terrible experience at Mu-in Hotel Kaohsiung

PT-BR:
Tive uma péssima experiência no Mu-in Hotel em Kaohsiung. Cheguei ao hotel às 21:32pm, dentro do horário de check-in (até 23h), e não havia ninguém na recepção. Entrei em contato e a atendente disse que meu cartão “não havia passado” e pediu meus dados pelo aplicativo, em vez de aceitar o pagamento presencial com cartão, como estava informado na reserva pelo Agoda.

Quando questionei, ela mudou a história dizendo que minha reserva “não existia”, mesmo eu tendo o comprovante. Para piorar, após eu enviar o print da reserva, ela cancelou a reserva na hora para sustentar a mentira.

Uma experiência completamente desonesta, insegura e nada profissional. Não me senti seguro em permanecer no local e acabei procurando outro hostel para passar a noite.
Compartilho esta review para alertar outros viajantes: fuja desse hotel!

⸻

EN:
I had a terrible experience at Mu-in Hotel in Kaohsiung. I arrived at 09:32 PM, within the check-in time (until 11 PM), and there was no one at the front desk. I contacted the staff, and the receptionist said my card “hadn’t gone through” and asked me to send my card details through the app, instead of simply allowing me to pay in person as stated in my Agoda booking.

When I questioned this, she changed her story, saying my reservation “didn’t exist,” even though I had the confirmation. To make it worse, after I sent a screenshot of my booking, she immediately canceled the reservation to sustain her lie.

It was a completely dishonest, unsafe, and unprofessional experience. I didn’t feel safe staying there and ended up looking for another hostel for the night.
Sharing this review to warn other travelers: avoid this hotel!

____________________________________

Updating the hotel's response. I also attached my receipts there in the updates. I've never used Booking.com to make a reservation. If this is an error on Agoda/Booking.com's part, not only me, but many others will have the same problem if you don't fix it. And it's a problem no one wants after spending hours on a plane to have the trip of their dreams. Since I booked through Agoda well in advance, I was informed that payment would be made at the hotel upon arrival. And I arrived aware of this, already with my card or cash to pay. You sent me a message through Agoda, informing me that the reception would only be open until 10:00 PM, and I replied that I arrived at the front of the hotel at 9:32 PM. So I was just going to arrive, pay, and that was it. But there was no one at the reception. When we got on the line, they said that card payment was not accepted and asked me to send the information through the app itself so they could process the payment. This is not common practice. I felt insecure about being asked for my card details through a messaging app that wasn't the one I used to book. But now there's no way you can fix the problem. I want to share my experience here, so that anyone who reads and understands the situation can decide whether it's worth the risk of going through the same situation. Thank you, and rest assured.

location is good, however the service was awful, first you aren’t allowed to check in until 3.30 which is insane, then the luggage storage was right in the reception at the main front doors, just a little built open cabinet, for anyone to walk in during the day and steal whatever they want, as you don’t need a keycard or code for the door until after 10. we politely asked the lady at reception, who was useless, if she would keep a small bag with just our passports and work laptop behind the desk for safety, she refused to do so and told us it had to be left out or taken with us. Lots of noise all throughout the nights from other rooms, people checking out etc, didn’t get one good nights sleep, then drilling starts at 9am which is perfect because who wants to sleep hey, right next to our room, non stop for hours. absolutely ridiculous 🤯😤not a care i’m the world to was given, rude and unacceptable from staff. oh and no elevator so just hope you aren’t on the second floor upwards, not practical for elderly, disabled or anyone really as we are a young couple in our late 20s and had to carry all our luggage up 3 flights of stairs
Decent stay for a decent price. Only stayed overnight. So far the cheapest stay for us when we went through Taiwan yet the best one out of all the stays.

The staff were very helpful, and the location was convenient, being close to a train station.

However, there were significant issues. There was no elevator, making it difficult to carry luggage, and the stairs were very steep and a bit dangerous to go up and down.

The room was extremely small, and when the window opened, it faced the wall of the next building just a meter away, with a noisy air conditioner.

The bathroom was poorly designed, with no separation between the shower and toilet, causing the entire area to get wet after a shower. The door was moldy, and there was no fridge or hangers for clothes or towels.

A large gap under the door allowed light to come in all night, and the soundproofing was poor, making it easy to hear noise from the corridor. Overall, I would not go back.

reviews.text:
Absolutely loved my stay at Brio Hotel Kaohsiung! The rooms are clean and well-equipped- the bidet in the bathroom is a huge plus for me, and they even provide a toilet spray that keeps everything smelling fresh!

Special thanks to Mr. Stanley Chang, who was incredibly helpful, friendly, and professional. Before we headed to the airport or we heading out, he even asked if we had enough water every single time- and said he would gladly give us more if we didn't. Such a warm and thoughtful gesture that really touched us!

The staff's food recommendations were excellent,  and the free light refreshments were a great bonus. I also really admire their eco-friendly initiative, encouraging guests with meaningful free gifts as a reward.

And one more thing- their room slippers are hands down the best I've ever worn in any hotel around the world. So soft, comfy, and well-made.

Highly recommend Brio Hotel for their exceptional service, comfort, and thoughtful details. Would love to stay here again!

If you're looking for an unforgettable stay in Kaohsiung, look no further than Brio Hotel. From the moment I walked in, I was blown away by the attention to detail and quality of service.

Rooms like a Dream: The rooms at Brio Hotel are truly a haven. Spacious, modern, and immaculately clean, with stunning design touches that make it feel like you're staying in a luxury retreat. The bed was incredibly comfortable, and the amenities made the entire experience feel top-notch.

Perfect Location: Located in a prime spot in Kaohsiung, the hotel offers easy access to the city's best attractions. Whether you're exploring the lively downtown or visiting nearby cultural sites, everything is just a short distance away, making it incredibly convenient for sightseeing.

Snack Bar Available 2x a Day: A nice touch that made a big difference during my stay. The snack bar, available twice a day, offered a great selection of light bites, perfect for grabbing something quick or relaxing after a day of exploration.

Amazing Breakfast: Brio Hotel's breakfast is nothing short of fantastic. A wide variety of fresh, delicious options that cater to every taste. From local Taiwanese favorites to international staples, you won't leave hungry.

Overall, Brio Hotel exceeded all my expectations, and I would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Kaohsiung. It offers excellent value for money with exceptional service and a memorable experience.

We had a fantastic stay at this hotel and it exceeded our expectations! The room was spacious, and we were especially happy to find a bidet spray in the toilet, which is something we always look for when booking a hotel.

The location is perfect, right in the center of Kaohsiung and just a short walk to the MRT, making it incredibly convenient to explore the city. It was also easy to find great food nearby and visit popular attractions.

The staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful (especially Stanley Chang), going the extra mile to recommend restaurants that suited our preferences. Another highlight was the hotel’s pantry, which offered free quick bites and snacks for guests. You will never go hungry staying here!

1. Place : very near with Formosa St. in RED LINE subway.

2. Formosa St. Is good location between HSR and Airport. No need transfer.

3. Room is so clean and perfect.

4. Kind and calm room.

5. No cafeteria. No toothbrush.

Google categorizes this hotel as a 3 star hotel. Honestly, that is a far stretch. It's more like a 2 star if even that. It's located on the 11th floor of a building with a security guard. However, based on the price vs location and greatvservice, I'd rate it around 3.5 stars.

Pros:
Yes, the location is great and very central in Kaohsiung. Therefore, access to the main Kaohsiung MRT is very convenient. It's also close to Liouhe night market and the Dome of Light.

The bathroom is quite large surprisingly especially given how small the room is.

Service was very friendly as well.

Cons:
The rooms are severely lacking. It's small, there are barely any tables to put your stuff on, no outlet plugs by both sides of the bed, no fridge, no microwave, walls are peeling and dirty. As most reviews have stated already, the walls are very thin with poor sound proofing. You hear every cough, every roar of laughter, every shouting and fighting match, every toilet flush, every fart and burp, etc. However, this didn't bother me personally as I was still able to sleep well despite these disruptions.

Wifi is available but it lags sometimes.

As mentioned earlier, the value is good overall but don't expect luxury.

CONS:

*Slow and small elevators. The hotel is on the 11th floor.
*Unit lacks a cabinet or clothes rack to hang your clothes.
*Unit lacks a desk top to put your bags or luggage on. It comes with a bed and a small desk good enough to hold bottled water and keys .
*There is no exhaust in the bathroom.
*You can hear conversations from the rooms adjacent to yours.
*This is not a 3-star hotel. But a 2-star hotel. Google states this place is a 3-star hotel.
*Reminds me of a hostel, but with a private bathroom
*Limited electric plugs
*Can feel claustrophobic, but the huge window helps.
*AC controller in local language hard to decipher
*No smart TV available. All TV in local language.
*Smoky entrance
*wifi clocked at 5 MBPS only.
* You will hear someone coughing or sneezing in the middle of the night as if they are in your room.. It woke me up to check if someone was indeed in my room.

PROS:
*very close to the night market (one block away)
*shower has plenty of hot water
*Bed is comfortable
*Large window view
*AC is a split AC system and more than sufficient
*Room cleaning service available
*One block or so from Fomosa Station
*Clean hallway and appears modern
*The lady at the front desk was kind. She was always asking us if we needed new towels, water bottles, or toilet paper. Very helpful.

If I rate this place based on the price, location, and service, it's 4 stars. But with the lack of storage areas for my clothes and bags, I gave it 3 stars, which isn't bad at all for this place.

reviews.text: Location was amazing very close to all our activities. We enjoyed our stay so much. The rooms were very clean and very spacious. Even just a standard room had a lot of room and the shower was amazing. Literally no complaint about this place at all as it was everything we were looking for. The rooms look just like the pictures

Cheap. Not the best but great for value. Includes breakfast. Quite dusty. It wasn't noisy while we were there. Parking was a bit confusing but figured it out. Bed was comfy. Shower was hot so that's good. It does suddenly get a bit hotter at times but still it was good. Wasn't a lot of food choices but maybe because we got here about 8pm.

After reading the reviews, booking a room, and staying here, I feel like I am definitely the minority in terms of opinion and feel compelled to share. First of all, the cleanliness left much to be desired. The shower was not cleaned well and there were stray hairs left in both the shower and bathroom.

My main complaint however has to do with the room layout. For whatever reason, the toilet and shower were housed in separate "booths" that were not completely walled off from the main room. Both of these booths were small, and the main room itself was small. This may be fine if you are staying here with a partner, but for anyone else it makes things extremely awkward. There's no "bathroom" to change in – you have to change in the shower and hope that your dry clothes don't get wet. Also, don't stay here if you don't want to hear your roommate's every start farts and pee streams all throughout the night. It is just too loud and disruptive.

Finally, the hotel for some reason only provided one small towel and one large towel per person. I was staying with two other people and when I asked for more towels, they said they were only able to provide two more. I've never seen a hotel with so few towels available.

Q21 Hotel located at a good area with many Taiwan tradition food and landmarks. The hotel itself is tidy, with new and trendy interior design. The front desk is helpful as well. Overall, I feel good staying here. One thing to note is that there is no closet in the room I selected, but then the room is large enough for me to open both of my suitcases. Which is fine and good as I am not staying long, but this could be a draw back for you.

reviews.text:
Right next to Kaohsiung station, very convenient for using the subway. Also a surprisingly quiet neighborhood. Staff were kind and friendly, the hotel itself is all together very clean and well organized.

The breakfast mostly consisted of Asian type dishes based on the customers nationality. Being a European I cannot really eat warm cooked food for breakfast, and the Western dishes were quite limited - bread, eggs, sausage and cheese and vegetables. I hope this could be improved as for long term stayers, this can be a bit repetitive.
And, our room's carpet had a huge stain on it that didn't seem like anyone really made an effor to clean it out.

Also, our fee was deducted from my bank account before arrival, but I had to pay once more once we actually arrived and be told that they will refund the first withdrawal within 2 weeks?? I've never encountered such a situation. It has been 1 week and I still haven't received my original payment back. Good thing I booked on booking and I have proof of both payments.
We very much enjoyed our stay in this hotel. Very clean and modern. Friendly and helpful staff. Free laundry. Breakfast was so delicious and amazing. Highly recommend!

Clean rooms and convenient location and very good value. Although the room did have a bit of a smell and the rooms can be kind of crammed. Location is amazing only across the street from the train station, however with construction it is kind of confusing to find your way. There was some homelessness in the area which did seem quite troublesome. Breakfast Buffet is well equipped and has a good selection.

Very easy to get to from Kaohsiung main station. Huge blue sign on roof. Staff was very helpful communicating directions from train station to hotel. Great breakfast, many options. Easy to use MRT to get around city. Loved having laundry facilities available at hotel.  Very happy with our choice if this hotel!

We stayed one night. The room without windows was bright and clean, but make sure you set an alarm to wake up because there is no natural light. The staff was very nice and the breakfast had a nice western and Taiwanese variety. There are homeless people several doors over but they didn't bother people. It was a good stay for a very good price. Also as another reviewer indicated, the bidet was very nice.

reviews.text:
We loved our stay at the "Good Hotel"! We've been so positively suprised, we didn't expected such a nice experience for the affordable price. The rooms were spotless clean,modern and had a beautiful design! The breakfast buffet was delicious, a mix of classic Taiwanese breakfast, but also international options.
And the service was so so caring and nice! It was one of my favorite hotels during our 3 weeks stay in Taiwan, I would definitely come back! ❤️

I was really impressed with this hotel in Kaohsiung. For the price, it completely exceeded my expectations. The room was extremely clean, the bed had great support and didn’t sink in, the blanket was very comfortable, and the bathroom even had a warm-water bidet. Shower pressure was excellent, and the TV had a wide range of channels.

The staff were friendly and very helpful, which made the stay even better. On top of that, they offered free breakfast, 24-hour free coffee and drinks, and even had a small public hot bath on level 2 where you can soak. The soundproofing of the room was also surprisingly good — I slept really well.

Overall, for this price, it’s hard to believe how much value you get. Honestly, now I’m worried my next stay at another hotel won’t match up to the cleanliness and comfort of this one!

Good Hotel is a great value if you’re staying in Kaoshiung. The location is very convenient, 10 min walk from MRT, or the Liuhe night market. There are restaurants and 711 nearby as well.

The room is very clean and rather spacious for Taiwan. The lobby has free coffee machines, and lots of chairs to lounge/work. There’s also 24hr bath house and coin laundry. There was also staff at the desk, and they were super nice.

Good Hotel is a great place to base out of when visiting Kaohsiung. I would definitely come back.

10/10 STAY HERE! The absolute best hotel in Kaohsiung for the price! The most memorable experience I have ever had.

I can’t tell you how wonderful this stay was! The hotel front desk staff was the most friendly and professional that I have ever encountered, including those compared to luxurious, five star hotels. The staff went above and beyond in ways I could have never imagined. Communication was outstandingly clear and helpful. Tom even offered me incredible advice for Penghu on his own initiative, and Victor helped me walk my luggage all the way to the train station when I checked out. So nice! Again, ABOVE AND BEYOND! The hotel room was spotless, perfectly clean and the public bath was absolutely fantastic. The laundry room was also a great perk and it did a great job, both wash and dry. The breakfast was also great to enjoy. I will absolutely stay here the next time I am in Kaohisung.

Stayed 3 nights in Kaohsiung and this hotel became the highlight of my trip. The room was spotless and thoughtfully organized, so it felt calm and comfortable every day. Every staff member I met was genuinely kind—thanks to them I made great memories here. I used both the gym and the bath and really appreciated how clean and well-kept they were. I even accidentally left a small mark on the gym ceiling, and the staff and manager reassured me with a smile and told me not to worry. Their warmth and professionalism turned an awkward moment into a grateful one. I’d happily stay here again.
